The third shift did not go down and in the Piast mine 11 members of the Strike Committee began a sit-in strike 650 metres below ground. Miners from the first and second shift went underground but they did not extract coal. NSW spokesman claims that during the first shift the Siersza, Silesia and Czeczot mines continued coal production. The company is losing approximately 80,000 tons of coal per day."  "Today (Friday) at noon the leadership of Miners' Solidarity and representatives of the Mining Industry Employers' Union will begin a second round of negotiations. So far the talks did not bring much effect. The Employers' Union has refused to correct last year's pay base and to pay each miner Zl 600 in compensation. However, representatives of employers did not exclude taking steps to liquidate the pay disproportions."

"Four thousand Gdansk Shipyard employees marched in the streets of Gdansk on Friday in protest against their employer's failure to pay them their April wages. They notified the local prosecutor's office about a crime committed by the government. Chanting "Down with the Reds," "Solidarity," "Bread and Jobs," and "Shipyard Is Alive," the protesters brought traffic in all of downtown Gdansk to a standstill. Although the demonstration was not authorised by the city authorities, the protesters had police protection. Outside an SLD deputy's office, they set off some firecrackers."

Protester Group Identity: Solidarity members representing education, science and culture
Notes: "On Saturday, over 2,000 Solidarity members representing education, science and culture staged a demonstration outside the Sejm and Cabinet Office (URM), demanding higher pay for civilian non-trading sector employees as well as amendments to the budget act to boost local expenditures on education. Present was Solidarity leader Marian Krzaklewski, who declared the entire union's support for those demands."

"Today in the morning, Gdansk Shipyard workers are scheduled to protest in front of the yard's gates against the government's decision not to restructure the yard. Shipyard Chairman Ryszard Goluch suggested that the protest is necessary because further talks in the matter are doomed to failure."

"Instead, protesters decided to stage a demonstration outside the Voivodship Office. The protest began a few days ago after 600 yard employees had not received their wages as promised. Wages have been paid out in instalments since January, with the yard highly indebted and receiving no orders. [...]"

"Medical personnel in a hospital on Warsaw's Solec Street staged a two-hour warning strike yesterday between 10 a.m. and noon. Examinations, operations and visits were suspended, and a rally was organised outside the hospital."  "Unionists demand across-the-board pay raises, back payments for hours spent on duty and increased government spending on the health service."

"Following similar protests organised in Warsaw and Radom earlier this month, yesterday health service employees staged a two-hour warning strike in health centres and hospitals throughout the Konin voivodship, Nowa Europa [No. 193, 21 August 1996 p.2] reports. Protesters are demanding that spending on the health sector be boosted to at least 6% of the GDP. This should be accompanied by a radical health service reform within the next two years and the government's respect for pay agreements signed. At the same time, a rally in support of the protest was staged in Poznan, where the same demands were repeated."

"Following a wave of protests organised in Warsaw, Poznan, Radom and Konin earlier this month, health service employees in the Czestochowa voivodship and in one hospital in Wroclaw staged a two-hour warning strike yesterday, Nowa Europa (No. 200, 29 August 1996, p.3) reports. Protesters are demanding higher expenditures on the health sector, a reduction of hospitals' debts and a departure from planned lay-offs. According to the organises of the protest, around 7,000 health service employees took part in the warning strike in Czestochowa, while 400 attended the rally in Wroclaw."

"Around 10,000 doctors from all over the country arrived in Warsaw last Friday for a silent march of protest and a demonstration outside the Sejm, demanding improvements in the condition of the health sector. In a resolution handed to Deputy Sejm Speaker Olga Krzyzanowska, they listed their demands to boost expenditures on the health sector to 6% of the GDP, introduce a national insurance reform in line with Solidarity's bill, adopt a law on the medical profession before the end of the year, secure decent working conditions and pay for doctors and raise pay in the health service before the end of the year."

"Last Friday, health sector employees staged a 30-minute picket outside the government clinic in Warsaw, announcing that regular pickets would be organised after October 22 in support of health service demands. Protests in the health sector have been escalating in recent months, and Solidarity is planning a nationwide protest on October 25."

"Last Friday, health sector employees throughout the country staged a protest action, including a strike organised in dozens of selected health service institutions in 14 voivodships. Rallies and pickets were held in health centres not selected for the strike, and the Solidarity union, which organised the protest, estimated that around 200,000 health service employees took part, including 60,000 strikers. Different forms of protest had been chosen in various regions of the country, although medical assistance was offered in emergencies."   "Meanwhile, government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska rejected accusations that the government was not prepared to negotiate with the health sector, and her position was echoed by Health Minister Jacek Zochowski, who told the press on Friday that the Cabinet had always been prepared to negotiate."

"Yesterday several farmers from the Wroclaw region picketed the Ministry of Agriculture and Food and the Sejm buildings in a protest organised by Rural Solidarity from Jelenia Gora. Farmers protested the state's failure to respond to farmer demands voiced in connection with losses incurred as a result of summer flooding. Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Food Jacek Soska (PSL) promised to ask the Council of Ministers to postpone the repayment of loans drawn by farmers in the spring of this year."

"Last Friday (Nov. 8) protesting doctors from the Solidarity union and from doctors' and nurses' self-regulation organisations picketed the Victoria Hotel in Warsaw where the Vth Conference of European Health Ministers was taking place. The picket was part of the wave of protests against the government's health policy which have recently swept through the medical community."

Protester Group Identity: the Committee for the Defence of the Shipyard
Notes: "Yesterday morning (Nov. 25), after a short rally held at the Stocznia Gdanska shipyard, about 1,500 shipyard workers marched on the Gdansk Voivodship Office. The protest was organised by the Committee for the Defence of the Shipyard, which had been established on the initiative of the Solidarity trade union. The workers' wanted the government to provide credit guarantees for shipbuilding contracts and to accelerate the restructuring of the yard."    "Several hundred workers started to occupy the Voivodship Office, and, in the end, more than one hundred stayed in the building overnight."

"Yesterday morning (Nov. 25), after a short rally held at the Stocznia Gdanska shipyard, about 1,500 shipyard workers marched on the Gdansk Voivodship Office. The protest was organised by the Committee for the Defence of the Shipyard, which had been established on the initiative of the Solidarity trade union. The workers' wanted the government to provide credit guarantees for shipbuilding contracts and to accelerate the restructuring of the yard. Several hundred workers started to occupy the Voivodship Office, and, in the end, more than one hundred stayed in the building overnight. "We are not going to leave until specific decisions are made in line with the government's commitments concerning the restructuring (of the yard). We also demand guarantees to be provided by the Treasury for the construction of five ships which have been ordered in the shipyard," Jerzy Borowczak, the shipyard's Solidarity leader, said."  "The government has not changed its position on the Gdansk shipyard. At its session yesterday, Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz insisted that the shipyard would receive no credit guarantees unless it found a bank ready to finance the construction of ships there."  "Seven Gdansk shipyard workers suspended their hunger strike last Friday and on Saturday most of the 150 workers who had for almost two weeks occupied the Voivodship Office in Gdansk left the building leaving behind representatives of local Solidarity and the Shipyard Defence Committee."

Protester Group Identity: the Independent Trade Union of Policemen
Notes: "Yesterday (Nov. 26), several hundred police officers demonstrated in front of the Sejm. Their demands included: a separate budget for the police, which would not be a part of the Interior Ministry's budget, salary increases to make the police pay scales equal to those in the military, as well as more funds for procurement to be obtained from government reserves. The protest was organised by the Independent Trade Union of Policemen. Police officers who were not on duty yesterday came from all over Poland to take part in the demonstration. The police protest started about a month ago, when national flags (the first sign of a work protest) were put up on police stations."

"Also on Wednesday, about two thousand people attended a rally organised by supporters of the protest in front of the Gdansk Voivodship Office which is currently under occupation by the shipyard workers. Participants of the rally included Solidarity unionists from Cracow's Huta Sendzimira steelworks, Poznan's engineering plant Cegielski, and Warsaw's tractor factory Ursus."

Protester Group Identity: Solidarity members from the PZL Swidnik aviation industry plant
Notes: "Solidarity members from the PZL Swidnik aviation industry plant are to picket the Sejm today in protest against the government's backpedalling on the plans to buy helicopters for the Polish armed forces next year."

Location of Protest: in front of the Sejm and the Cabinet Office
Notes: "About three thousand Solidarity unionists held three parallel demonstrations in front of the Sejm and the Cabinet Office yesterday (Dec. 18). Jars with red paint and firecrackers were thrown at the Cabinet Office, breaking several windows."  "Solidarity's power industry section was the first to begin its demonstration. The unionists picketed the Sejm protesting against the new energy law which they believed to be disastrous for Poland. Marian Krzaklewski, Solidarity chairman, announced more protests to be held next year unless the situation in the power industry changed."  "The loudest demonstration was the one held by Solidarity unionists from the Stocznia Gdanska shipyard. In the early afternoon several hundred shipyard workers, accompanied by representatives of coal miners and workers from Warsaw's tractor factory Ursus, arrived in front of the Sejm. Marian Krzaklewski led them towards the Cabinet Office. The demonstrators were joined by a group of activists from the Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP)."

"The protest committee established by traders from one of Poland's largest market places in Bia3ystok, has decided to block the Polish-Belarusian border crossing in Ku nica Bia3ostocka today (February 9). The traders claim that the government is ignoring their protests against the stricter border controls introduced by Poland at the end of last year, which have reduced the number of visitors coming from Russia and Belarus, thereby dramatically affecting the sales of Polish open-air markets."

"Almost 2,000 workers from the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard blocked roads here today, while in Warsaw the Solidarity union planned nationwide protests to preserve their jobs. The demonstrators set tires and paint barrels afire, sending plumes of smoke over Gdansk while traffic jams stretched for miles out of the city center."

"Hundreds of laid-off workers hurled bricks and red paint today at the Government party headquarters in Gdansk to protest the closing of the bankrupt shipyard where the Solidarity movement was born. Chanting "Down with Communists!" the workers hung a pig's head dipped in red paint on the building and burned an effigy of Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz. The roughly 1,000 protesters also set fire to piles of tires in front of the provincial governor's office, about 900 feet away. In Warsaw, protesters blocked the office of Treasury Minister Miroslaw Pietrewicz, hurling chairs and flower pots at riot police officers before they were dispersed with tear gas."

"Around one thousand doctors and patients marched through the streets of Wroclaw yesterday in protest against the financial condition of the health service, and similar marches were staged in Jelenia Gora and Walbrzych."

"Over 500 shopkeepers and private tradesmen protested in Warsaw yesterday (April 17) against the city authorities's policy towards small traders and businesses."  "The protest was mainly staged by merchants from the Central district and owners of small market stalls and kiosks on Marszalkowska St., stalls which the city authorities have decided, are to be razed to the ground with the construction of the subway station at Plac Defilad square."

"Warsaw: Seven thousand Polish doctors marched on parliament in the latest of a year-long series of pay protests (Pat Koza writes). The doctors want the Government to triple their salaries, which average Pounds 216 a month, and more funds for the health service."  "Nearly 10,000 doctors marched in silence through the streets of Warsaw last Friday in protest against low spending on the health service, "scandalously low pay" and the health insurance act, which they perceive as "consolidating the present inefficient health care system."

Location of Protest: the Polish-German border crossing of Jedrzychowice-Ludwigsdorf near Zgorzelec
Notes: "Two hundred farmers blocked a road leading to the Polish-German border crossing of Jedrzychowice-Ludwigsdorf near Zgorzelec, between 11 a.m. and 1 p.m., yesterday in protest against the government's agricultural policy."   "Rural Solidarity, which organised the protest, plans to embark on a collective dispute with the government and press for the impeachment of officials responsible for a decision allowing the duty-free importation of some grains and food."

Location of Protest: in front of the Voivodship Office in Zamosc
Notes: "Over 100 farmers from the Zamosc gmina and the Solidarity committee of the local sugar company protested yesterday (June 25) in front of the Voivodship Office in Zamosc against the government's agricultural policy."

"Yesterday (Sept.11) approximately 1,500 workers from sugar-processing plants demonstrated in Warsaw in front of the Agriculture and Food, and Treasury Ministry buildings and the Premier's Chancellery in protest against the difficult economic situation of the sugar-processing industry."

"An estimated 200 anaesthesiologists from 28 hospitals in and around Warsaw yesterday joined the hunger strike begun last week by seven physicians in Tarnow, who have now been hospitalised. On Monday, anaesthesiologists in 37 hospitals in the Katowice region joined the protest, with 35 doctors currently conducting a hunger strike there."   "Nine anaesthetists in Sieradz voivodship joined in the hunger strike yesterday conducted by doctors throughout the country, with 6 anaesthetists in Tarnow and an estimated 200 in and around Warsaw continuing their hunger strike. In Katowice, around 300 anaesthetists are taking part in the protest, with 35 of them currently on a hunger strike."   "Anaesthesiologists throughout the country are now escalating their protest after the Wednesday negotiations with Health Ministry representatives ended in a fiasco. In Warsaw and Katowice, anaesthesiologists are continuing their hunger strike, which spread to Radom yesterday and is expected to begin in Cracow, Ostroleka and Chelm today. A further escalation of the protest is planned on Monday, when physicians in five more regions are to join in the hunger strike, demanding higher pay and better working conditions."  "An estimated 200 anaesthetists in Lublin, Zamosc, Lodz, Suwalki, Bialystok and Lomza have joined in the ongoing protest of physicians after Tuesday's talks between government negotiators and the protesters ended in a fiasco. This means that the protest is now continuing in 16 voivodships and is expected to spread to other regions. Plans for this escalation are being discussed by anaesthetists this weekend."

Location of Protest: the Muszyna railway station in Southern Poland
Notes: "Several dozen farmers from the Wroclaw region yesterday blocked a train carrying imported grain at the Muszyna railway station in Southern Poland to protest against farm produce imports from Western Europe. The farmers want Poland to stop all imports of grain, beef, pork, feed and other farm produce and warned they would aggravate their protest should the government reject their demands."

"The NSZZ Solidarity farm union held a demonstration in Warsaw yesterday. A group of several hundred protesters started at the seat of Farmers' Solidarity National Council and marched to the Witos monument, then to the Sejm and to the Prime Minister's Chancellery."

Location of Protest: outside the Voivodship Office in Lodz
Notes: "An estimated 3,000 nurses from all over the country attended a march and demonstration staged yesterday outside the Voivodship Office in Lodz in protest against low pay.  Their demands, which are to be passed on the president and premier, include a halt to planned pay increases for anaesthesiologists. "There should be no preferential treatment for just one professional group, as we are a part of the system," nurses explained."

"Despite the proclamation of official mourning in Slupsk, this northern town saw more rioting last night, with angry youngsters threatening to take revenge on the police for the Saturday death of a 13-year-old boy."  "Chanting "blood for blood," hundreds of teenagers clashed with police in rioting spurred by the police killing of a 13-year-old basketball fan.   Twenty officers were injured and 42 young people were arrested in the overnight violence in the northern city of Slupsk. It was the second night of violence since the teenager was killed Saturday. The teenagers -- numbering 500 according to police and 1,000 according to Polish media -- gathered outside police headquarters late Monday before rampaging through the streets, throwing stones, damaging police cars and setting garbage containers on fire."

Location of Protest: road leading to the Polish-Russian border crossing in Bezledy (Olsztyn voivodship)-Bagrationovsk (Kaliningrad district)
Protester Group Identity: inhabitants of the nearby Polish border regions
Notes: "In the early hours of the morning yesterday (January 15), over one hundred cars and trucks staged a blockade of the road leading to the Polish-Russian border crossing in Bezledy (Olsztyn voivodship)-Bagrationovsk (Kaliningrad district). By the evening, the queue of trucks waiting to cross the border was three kilometres long and continued to grow. Only vehicles carrying perishable goods were let across the crossing.     The blockade was organised by inhabitants of the nearby Polish border regions who protested against the recently introduced border crossing procedures which, in their opinion, had stripped them of work and income by hindering unregistered trade. The list of their desiderata was delivered to the border guards, the customs administration and the police."

"More than 1,500 traders staged a picket of the Voivodship Office in Bialystok to protest against the new border procedures hindering unregistered trade with Belarus and Russia. "The effects of the new regulations will be felt not only by traders, but by half of the city and the region," claimed the chairman of the Bialystok Business Initiative, who organised the protest. "We have also received words of support from entrepreneurs from all over Poland."

"Yesterday (Jan. 28) around 2,000 members of the National Trade Union of Nurses and Obstetricians marched through the streets of Warsaw demanding pay raises of up to 150 percent of the national monthly average wage and increased spending on the health care system. The protesting nurses met with Health Minister Wojciech Maksymowicz who said that any significant pay raises will be possible only after conducting a systemic reform of the health service and promised to publicly disclose its details within a month."

Location of Protest: the roads leading to the Polish-Belarusian border
Notes: "Traders from the open-air market in Bia3ystok blocked one of the roads leading to the Polish-Belarusian border crossing in Ku nica Bia3ostocka yesterday (February 9) morning, but traffic has now been resumed. A counter-blockade was staged several kilometres from the crossing by truck drivers who had to wait more than thirty hours to pass through the border. "

"Farmers from Rural Solidarity held a demonstration in Warsaw yesterday afternoon (March 4) to protest the 10-year transition period proposed for Polish agriculture after accession to the European Union. They claim the arrangement will deprive them of the benefits, including production subsidies, enjoyed by EU farmers under the Common Agricultural Policy."  "Police estimate the number of participants at 1,500, though Roman Wierzbicki, Rural Solidarity chairman, claims a turn-out of about 3,000."

"Around four thousand people staged a demonstration in central Opole yesterday to protest against the government's plans to liquidate the Opole voivodship as a result of the administrative reform.  Before the demonstration, local government leaders met at the townhall and adopted a resolution demanding that Poland's new administrative division should include the Opole voivodship. A number of parliamentarians present at the meeting, including three politicians from Solidarity Elections Action (AWS), promised they would vote against changing Opole's status in the Sejm."

Location of Protest: outside the Ministry of Finance and parliament (Warsaw)
Protester Group Identity: union members from Warsaw's Ursus tractor plant
Notes: "About 6,000 union members from Warsaw's Ursus tractor plant, aided by coal miners from Silesia, demonstrated outside the Ministry of Finance and parliament to protest against the government's policies on subsidising the factory and on preferential loans to farmers for the purchase of tractors. Demonstrators demanded government support for the plant, including measures such as higher duty on imported components for the assembly of tractors and a ban on the registration of second hand imported tractors. The enterprise faces daunting financial conditions and blames state officials and the media."

"Last Friday (April 3) the OPZZ labour federation staged a huge protest march in Warsaw against the policy of Buzek's Cabinet. The march was supported by leader of the Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) Leszek Miller, leader of the Polish Socialist Party Piotr Ikonowicz and of the Labour Union Marek Pol.  The marchers demanded the dismissal of deputy premier and Finance Minister Leszek Balcerowicz, talks with Premier Buzek and the fulfilment of 47 demands, including the holding of a referendum on the administrative reform. They accused the government of failing to consult social reform projects and planned price increases with trade unions."
"More than 100 environmentalists protested near the village of Gogolin on Friday against the route of the A-4 motorway under construction, which  intersects the Gora Sw. Anny landscape park."

"A group of 51 doctors is continuing their hunger strike at a hospital in Kalisz, while 28 surgeons conducting a hunger strike at a hospital in Plock decided to escalate their protest yesterday and they are now refusing liquids as well, in an attempt to force the hospital administration into meeting their pay demands. "We are desperate, as the administration as well as voivodship authorities have not come up with any new proposals for days, remaining either deaf to our demands or incompetent," surgeons explain. As a consequence, protesters have sent a letter to the Minister of Health, asking for mediation."

"More than 1,000 unionists demonstrated outside a hotel in Szczyrk where the Sejm Committee on the Economy gathered for an itinerant meeting to discuss the role of coal in the nation's energy policy. Protesters carried a coffin to symbolise the agonising condition of the coal sector and chanted slogans against Solidarity Election Action (AWS) and Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Leszek Balcerowicz."

Protester Group Identity: the Committee in Defence of Health Care Reform
Notes: "An estimated 500 doctors and nurses picketed Parliament yesterday in protest against the version of the health insurance reform drafted by the government and protests were also staged throughout the country as hospitals and health care centres demonstrated their solidarity by offering medical assistance in emergencies only. The protest was coordinated by the Committee in Defence of Health Care Reform, which organises all the unions and associations representing the medical profession. The Committee is demanding higher pay for health care employees as well as higher health insurance contributions, arguing that the latter should be boosted to 11 percent in lieu of the 7.5 percent the government is proposing.

Location of Protest: the Polish-German border crossing at Kolbaskowo
Notes: "Yesterday (July 8), approximately 100 farmers blocked the Polish-German border crossing at Kolbaskowo, meanwhile at a rail crossing on the Polish-Czech border at Zebrzydowice, around 200 farmers from Rural Solidarity boarded a train and spilled 500 tons of imported Hungarian grain onto the tracks."

Protester Group Identity: the National Union of Farmers' Organisations, NSZZ Farmers' Solidarity and the Samoobrona Trade Union
Notes: "On Friday some 10,000 farmers demonstrated in Warsaw against the government's agricultural policy. For several hours protesters blocked the main streets of the city. Police were forced to use truncheons, tear gas and water canons in the two main clashes with demonstrators.     The demonstration was organised by the National Union of Farmers' Organisations, NSZZ Farmers' Solidarity and the Samoobrona Trade Union. The protesters led a she-goat which was meant to symbolise the poverty of Polish agriculture and be a gift to deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance Leszek Balcerowicz; Balcerowicz milks farmers, so let him milk the she-goat, farmers shouted. Eggs, milk cartons and yoghurts were tossed at the ministry building."

"Angry farmers spilled nearly 650 tons of Hungarian grain near the border crossing in Muszyna, southern Poland, yesterday, August 3, and threatened to block the roads at several hundred strategic locations between noon and 4 p.m today. The estimated 60-100 farmers, from Rural Solidarity, drove to the border crossing in two buses and four cars. The two railway police officers patrolling the station could only look on as the destruction took place.

Protester Group Identity: Rural Solidarity movement and the National Union of Farmers' Societies and Organizations
Notes: Thousands of farmers continued to block roads in a protest over cheap agricultural imports. The farmers, whose protests have been declared illegal, say the Government allows Western meat and grain imports to lower prices for Polish produce. Farmers are demanding a total ban on imports. The Government says that would violate international agreements

Chanting "thieves, thieves" and burning an effigy of Poland's Prime Minister, tens of thousands of farmers and workers marched through Warsaw today to press the Government for better wages and job security. Exhausted by 10 years of economic difficulty in the transition from Communism, protesters accused Prime Minister Jerzy Buzek's administration of ignoring the nation's problems and called for the presidential election, now set for 2001, to be moved up. The leader of the radical farmers, Andrzej Lepper, urged the Government to resign, saying it was working under "the dictate of the rotten West." About 30,000 people marched in the rally, though the farm unions and labor groups that organized the event had predicted three times that number. They later said they had cut back on participants to avoid overburdening Warsaw's residents. But leaders of Mr. Buzek's Solidarity party called the low turnout a blow for the leftist opposition.

In Poland slow-moving trucks snarled traffic, while in the largest protests yet in the Netherlands truckers stopped traffic across the country and handed in a petition for lower diesel ahead of next week's budget.

About 10,000 Poles led by the Solidarity bloc's presidential candidate marched in downtown Warsaw today to protest the veto of a bill aimed at giving state-owned apartments and farmland to their current users. The demonstration was organized by Marian Krzaklewski, who is trailing badly in public opinion polls behind President Aleksander Kwasniewski heading into the election Sunday.

Tens of thousands of trade unionists rallied in Warsaw yesterday to protest against the left-wing government's proposed relaxation of employment laws, which they fear will add to unemployment, now running at a record three million. The Solidarity rally by workers from shipyards, steelworks and coal mines was the union's first show of strength since the right-wing government it backed was swept from power by the reformed communists in elections last September.

Hundreds of farmers occupied the agriculture ministry in Warsaw yesterday in protest at a slump in produce prices. Led by the maverick politician Andrzej Lepper, they tried to reach the office of the agriculture minister but were turned back by riot police. "The government has cheated the farmers," said Mr Lepper, the leader of the populist Self-Defence party.

Demonstrators led by the populist farmers' leader, Andrzej Lepper, tried to block roads to protest against soaring unemployment and rural poverty. The police, who were out in force, prevented Mr Lepper's followers blocking the roads as they have in the past. The protests were "a total flop", a police spokesman claimed .
More than 1,000 trade union demonstrators outside the central bank chanted "Balcerowicz must go" in reference to Leszek Balcerowicz, the author of the "shock therapy" reforms of the Nineties.

Farmers who fear European Union competition will ruin them staged a protest in Warsaw yesterday despite a government appeal to tone down protests before a referendum on joining the EU. About 2,500 farmers marched behind a truck with an effigy of Leszek Miller, the Prime Minister, and gallows with the inscription: "Today the Farmers, Tomorrow the Government".

About 20,000 trade unionists marched in Warsaw to protest against government policies they blame for economic stagnation and record unemployment. The protest, organized by the Solidarity union, highlighted the declining popularity of the left-wing minority government just weeks before a referendum on whether Poland should join the European Union in 2004. The protesters demanded urgent measures to cut unemployment, which at nearly 19 percent is at its highest level since the 1989 fall of Communism.

WARSAW endured some of the worst rioting seen since the fall of communism yesterday, as demonstrating miners affiliated to the Solidarity trade union attacked buildings and left a a trail of destruction. At least 40 policemen were injured when hundreds of miners broke away from a demonstration against proposed pit closures. Police guarding government offices were attacked with petrol bombs, cobblestones and fireworks.

About 1,000 homosexuals in Warsaw rallied outside City Hall to protest the mayor's decision to ban an annual gay parade. The mayor, Lech Kaczynski, canceled the parade and a planned counterdemonstration for security reasons

Polish riot police used water cannons and tear gas yesterday to disperse a protest by coal miners who are demanding an extension of retirement benefits. Fifty protesters were detained and 11 people, mostly police officers, were injured near the parliament buildings. A protest organiser apologised for the violence, but claimed victory after deputies agreed to consider extending early retirement rights for miners, which could cost up to å£4.4bn over five years " nearly 3 per cent of Poland's GDP " and delay plans to adopt the euro.

Thousands of demonstrators took to the streets yesterday to demand a complete ban on abortion, even in cases of rape or incest. At two separate rallies, "pro-life" supporters demonstrated their support for a tightening of Poland's abortion law, which is already among the most restrictive in the EU.

Polish miners raised protest banners yesterday in support of hundreds of nurses who are demonstrating for more pay. State medical workers say they have been left behind by the rapid rise in salaries for other professions, partly the result of a booming economy since Poland joined the European Union in 2004 and because of emigration that has led to a tight labour market.

Hundreds of riot police officers, some of them on horses, fought pitched battles in central Warsaw on Tuesday with traders resisting eviction from a bazaar seen as a symbol of the raw capitalism that flourished in the early 1990s. The police used water cannons against the protesters, who fought back with stones, bricks and sticks. The authorities want to dismantle the building and erect a museum of modern art in its place. Under a court order, the traders were to have left by Sunday.

Angry crowds in Poland have protested over plans to bury President Lech Kaczynski and his wife in Wawel Cathedral in Krakow, which is normally reserved for poets and kings. The couple were among scores of senior national figures who were killed in an air crash in Russia on Saturday. Hundreds of demonstrators took to the streets of Krakow, and thousands have joined an internet campaign protesting against the plan. The burial site was chosen by the late President's family and endorsed by the Polish Catholic Church. Brandishing placards that asked: "Is Kazcynski a King?" the protesters marched around the cathedral chanting "Krakow says no!" Thousands of people also visited a Facebook page entitled "No to Kaczynski at the Wawel".
Protesters in Warsaw, including miners and shipyard workers, marched to prime minister Donald Tusk s office chanting: No to budget cuts! and Yes to job protection and economic growth!

Although Poland remains staunchly pro-European, there have been stirrings of discontent, particularly in the main opposition Law and Justice Party led by Jaroslaw Kaczynski, the former prime minister. A rally against closer European integration led by Mr. Kaczynski drew about 3,000 people to the streets of Warsaw on Tuesday, according to a police estimate cited by The Associated Press.

Warsaw Thousands of Poles protested outside Parliament against plans to raise the retirement age to 67 for all, from 60 for women and 65 for men. Donald Tusk, the Prime Minister, said the move would increase pensions and cut state debt. (AP)

Hundreds of Polish trade union members protesting against plans to raise the retirement age chained together barriers meant to keep them out of Parliament on Friday, locking lawmakers in for more than an hour. ''We will decide when they will leave,'' a Solidarity trade union leader, Piotr Duda, said. ''At least for once we will decide something instead of them.'' The union members took their action after lawmakers voted to raise the retirement age to 67 for most Poles, part of the government's efforts to cut state debt, maintain growth and maintain investor confidence. Until now, women were allowed to retire at age 60 and men at 65.

Hundreds of gay men, lesbians and their supporters marched through the capitals of Poland and Latvia, demanding more rights in Eastern European societies where they still face high levels of intolerance. About 2,500 people turned out in Warsaw, while about 400 braved rain and hail to march in Riga. The demonstrations are among many gay-pride events taking place in June across Europe and elsewhere

While thousands of Polish labor union members marched through Warsaw on Thursday, a member of the governing party defected, pushing the center-right government of Prime Minister Donald Tusk to the brink of losing its parliamentary majority amid intensifying popular discontent. The protests, which began on Wednesday and are set to continue into Saturday, reflect Poles' growing dissatisfaction with the economy. Poles are also showing increasing fatigue with Mr. Tusk, who came to power in 2007. About 23,000 protested on Wednesday, and organizers are predicting 60,000 on Saturday, according to Gazeta Wyborcza, a leading newspaper.

Poland was the only European country not to head into recession at the worst of the global crisis in 2009 - a so-called "island of green" in a continent of red. The last time Italy tried to grant legal rights to same-sex couples, Pope Benedict XVI helped lead the charge that stopped it. But as Italian lawmakers opened debate Thursday on a new civil unions bill, the Vatican under Pope Francis is taking a very different approach.  In Italy, the Catholic reaction to the measure has been split. Hundred of thousands of Italians - including Catholics - demonstrated last weekend in an unprecedented display of support for the bill. At the same time, the opposition - led by conservative Catholic groups - plans to stage a "Family Day" protest on Saturday aimed at stopping the legislation.  Backed by the center-left government of Prime Minister Matteo Renzi, the new Italian bill comes one year after the European Court of Human Rights ruled in favor of several same-sex Italian couples who said that Italy was violating their human rights by denying them legal benefits. Gay rights activists describe the bill as a compromise - a pragmatic acknowledgment that full marriage rights probably would still fail in largely Catholic Italy.

An Italian senator has called for a boycott of Ikea after the Swedish chain organised a nationwide event supporting gay marriage to coincide with a demonstration in Rome held to oppose it.  The Ikea event on Saturday began as thousands gathered in Rome's Circus Maximus to protest against a government bill allowing gay unions, which is to be voted on in the Italian senate later this month. Speakers at the rally criticised a clause in the bill that would allow a partner in a same-sex union to adopt the biological child of the other partner. They claimed that it opened the door to gay adoption.

Italian senators voted last night to back gay unions but the last-minute ditching of a clause allowing same-sex couples to adopt children provoked a stinging rebuke from gay and lesbian groups.  A group of 28 Italian LGBT groups denounced the law as a sell-out, saying: "The senate has written an ugly page in the story of civil rights in our country." After a demonstration outside the senate on Wednesday, they promised another protest march next month.

"One town in Italy attempted to answer that question last December, when it introduced a new ordinance to regulate pizzamakers and other restauranteurs using wood-fired ovens.   San Vitaliano, a small town outside Naples, has banned the use of wood-fired stoves not equipped with filters that reduce air pollutants.  The announcement was met with outrage from pizzeria owners and residents, who held protests and argued that wood-burning stoves were not the ""real cause"" of the town's high pollution levels, the BBC reports. Mayor Antonio Falcone, who introduced the ordinance, became known as ""the anti-pizza mayor."""

Thousands march for gay rights in Italy, Poland, Croatia: Several thousand people marched Saturday in colorful gay pride events in Italy, Poland and Croatia urging support for minority rights in the mostly Catholic nations. The parades in Poland and Croatia come amid mounting right-wing sentiments that pose new challenges to gay rights activists. In Italy, however, the gay pride celebration comes after lawmakers granted some legal rights to same-sex couples.

"Residents of a tiny Italian fishing village erected barricades to prevent 20 asylum seekers including a heavily pregnant woman and eight children from moving in.  Gorino on the Adriatic coast is one of hundreds of small communities in Italy that have been called on to house migrants after the arrival of 155,000 from Africa since January. Officials have tried to spread out the new arrivals to avoid ghettoes forming in cities.  However, when a bus arrived carrying the group of female asylum seekers, more than 200 people set up crates to block the only road into Gorino. When the vehicle was forced to turn back they cheered and celebrated with wine.  ""They are bringing women but the women have their men,"" said Stefania, a villager. ""We are here for hours during the day without our husbands at home, so this is frightening.""  Matteo Renzi, the prime minister, was swift to criticise the protest. However, he warned that Italy could not handle another year of migrant arrivals and attacked countries such as Hungary that have refused to take part in an EU plan to relocate migrants."

"Seven days before a referendum that could end the career of Matteo Renzi, the Italian prime minister, and plunge Europe into further turmoil, tens of thousands of people marched against him. They were encouraged by an American-style social media campaign that has been accused of distorting the truth.  Protesters meeting in Piazza del Popolo in Rome said that Mr Renzi's proposals to streamline politics by scrapping the powers of the senate, which will be put to the vote on Sunday, would cut essential checks and balances on the government."

"Riot police were out in force to protect Matteo Renzi in Naples last night as he gave one of his final speeches before a referendum that could signal the end of his meteoric but brief political career.  As a hotbed of protest against his two-year government, the southern city was always going to be a tough rally, with even the local mayor urging his people to vote ""no"" on Sunday to the prime minister's plans to speed up the country's sluggish law-making by reining in the power of the senate.  On the streets, however, activists for the ""yes"" vote were also making themselves heard and promising to prove the polls wrong."

Tensions were high yesterday in Palermo, where riot police charged protesters carrying a burning effigy of Mr Renzi. "If 'yes' wins, Italy will be the strongest country in Europe," Mr Renzi said at a rally, promising that, if he got his way, his next move would be to block the EU's budget until surrounding countries took in more of the 170,000 migrants who have sailed to Italy this year.

"The sun-dappled olive groves of Italy's deep south have become a battleground as riot police and protesters clash over the building of an ambitious gas pipeline.  Tension over the uprooting of centuries-old olive trees to make way for the pipeline boiled over on Tuesday, as police armed with batons and shields charged hundreds of protesters in an olive grove in the region of Puglia, in the heel of the Italian boot.  Protesters have called for it to be re-routed so as to avoid an area where people rely on tourism and olive oil for their livelihoods.  The clashes broke out near the village of Melendugno, south of the elegant Baroque town of Lecce, where protesters are trying to block the uprooting of hundreds of olive trees .  Scuffles broke out as police tried to move demonstrators away from the construction site. Protesters threw stones and bottles at the police and several people were injured.  The digging up of the olive trees was temporarily suspended but later resumed. ""Our battle is entirely legitimate and we have always wanted it to be peaceful, but the response of the police was disproportionate,"" said Gianluca Maggiore, one of the protest leaders.  The regional government of Puglia is opposed to the pipeline, with Michele Emiliano, the centre-Left governor, branding it ""illegal"".  Protesters, including politicians and local mayors, are opposed to the uprooting of hundreds of olive trees along the route of the pipeline."

"THOUSANDS of protesters in Tirana last night called on Albania's leadership to adopt reforms while hundreds scaled the walls of foreign embassies seeking refuge. The Austria Press Agency said that Albanian police with truncheons attacked pro-democracy demonstrators. Ten thousand people gathered in a central square as the Communist party's central committee held a meeting."

"Hundreds of students chanting "Reforms!" and "No dictatorship!" clashed with the police today in the Albanian capital, Tirana, in a protest unparalleled under Communist rule, diplomats said. The diplomats, reached by telephone from Vienna, said the clash had occurred when riot policemen had surrounded 500 to 1,000 students marching from their campus toward the city center and charged them with batons."

"AS STUDENT sit-in protests continued yesterday, thousands of people gathered in Tirana, the Albanian capital, to found the country's first nominally independent opposition party. But the continuing unrest illustrated that President Alia has failed to satisfy demands for multiparty elections and other reforms. One student has died in the protests, which began on Sunday, apparently because of power failures at a student dormitory. At least three other students have been seriously injured in clashes between police and about 9,000 students."

"Rioters attacked public buildings in the northern Albanian city of Shkoder today, wounding several policemen, the official press agency reported. There were also reports of violence in the industrial town of Kavaje, a scene of anti-Communist demonstrations in the spring and summer. Police and army units were deployed in Shkoder and Kavaje to curb rioters, the press agency and witnesses said."  "As Albanian students continued their demonstrations workers from the factories of Tirana yesterday came out in support of the students. Security police guarding public buildings, including television and radio, have been reinforcd in the capital, according to witnesses."

"Anti-Communist demonstrators were out in force in Albanian cities today for the fourth successive day, the official press agency and people reached by telephone in Albania said. But there were no reports of violence after three nights in which rioters attacked Communist Party headquarters and monuments in Elbasan and Shkoder and damaged bookstores and other shops in Kavaje and Durres. There were also unconfirmed reports of demonstrations in the southern coastal resort city of Saranda, an area where ethnic Greeks are numerous. At noon today, according to a caller from Elbasan, a large crowd assembled in front of the district party headquarters, demanding the release of 100 demonstrators arrested on Friday night during clashes in which six police officers were wounded. They were driven back by police units, he said. Last Sunday, thousands of Tirana university students began demonstrations against the Communist regime in the capital, and on Tuesday won concessions from President Ramiz Alia, who endorsed the establishment of opposition political parties for the first time and dismissed five members of the Politburo."

"Thousands of Albanian students gathered in Tirana today for the second day of a strike organized to demand economic change and the resignation of the Communist Government, an opposition party spokesman said. The spokesman, Genc Polo of the seven-week-old Democratic Party, said about 8,000 students, shouting "Down with the dictatorship!" and "Resign!" thronged a square on the university campus in Tirana for a meeting that lasted more than two hours."

"With thousands of Albanians demonstrating in the streets of the capital for an end to Communist rule and with the country's economy in a shambles, President Ramiz Alia began today to try to form a crisis government."

"Albanian police yesterday arrested more than 200 people after tens of thousands of protesters tore down statues of late Stalinist dictator Enver Hoxha last week, an opposition leader said. Some of those arrested were beaten before being freed and an unknown number remain in jail, said Arben Imami, a Democratic Party leader reached by telephone in Tirana, Albania."

"Army units fired today on anti-Communist demonstrators protesting election results by sitting in the main square of this northern Albanian city, killing three of them and wounding 30. Enraged by the killings, thousands of young men surrounded two armored personnel carriers stationed in front of Shkoder's Communist Party headquarters and set them afire with gasoline bombs."

"Albanians marched through Tirana yesterday on the third day of a general strike. The strike was called by the country's independent Trade Union Federation to press demands for wage increases, and for a full investigation into the killing of four Democratic Party members. Similar demonstrations were reported throughout the country."

"The police were called in to disperse a rally of more than 10,000 people yesterday in Tirana held in support of hunger-striking miners. The demonstrators hurled stones while the police used water cannons. The general strike by the miners began May 16 and has paralyzed the Albanian economy."  Albanian government resigned after these protests and the general strike.

"About 20,000 Albanians rallied in Tirana today to celebrate the first anniversary of pro-democracy protests that ended more than four decades of Stalinism in Europe's poorest country. But the mood was dampened by a lack of heating in many cities as a cold wave swept the country, increasing the misery of a weary population already suffering from chronic food shortages and a paralyzed Government."
"More than 20,000 people demonstrated today at an anti-Communist rally, demanding the resignation of President Ramiz Alia and pledging to support the opposition in the next general election."
"Wage protest TIRANA - About 20,000 workers converged on central Tirana yesterday to demand higher wages and social reform in Albania, a country suffering from chronic food shortages."

"Food riots in Albania TIRANA, Albania: Thousands of people were reported massing in Durres yesterday in an apparent effort to commandeer ships and flee this impoverished country after the latest outbreak of food riots. Radio Tirana said one youth was killed and 20 people, including 16 police officers, were injured as rioters looted and burned two food warehouses in Peqin. The government said earlier six people were injured. At least four people have died and scores have been injured in fighting over food since Tuesday."

"TIRANA (Reuter) - The Albanian government said yesterday it was ready to order security forces into the town of Polican, where workers in the country's only armaments factory have armed themselves since Tuesday with guns and explosives to protest at job losses. The workers set the factory's offices on fire, besieged the town hall and called for the government to resign."

"Thousands of supporters of Albania's opposition Socialist Party demonstrated in Tirana yesterday in protest at the arrest of the party's chairman, former prime minister Fatos Nano, on charges of abuse of power. About 20,000 people demanding Mr. Nano's release and the government's resignation marched on Scanderbeg Square in the centre of the Albanian capital. Police detained dozens of demonstrators. But there was no violence as police managed to keep the protesters away from a crowd of government supporters."

"ETHNIC Greeks, in a defiant display of nationalism, poured on to the streets of southern Albania's impoverished villages yesterday to commemorate one of Greece's great national holidays. With blue and white Greek flags the order of the day, the celebration took place against a backdrop of strained relations between Athens and Tirana. The anniversary not only marked Greece's entry into the second world war, but also the day Greeks chose to fight Italian fascist forces invading from Albania. Ethnic Greeks were quick to describe the celebration as a protest demonstration."

"About 2,500 former political prisoners began a hunger strike yesterday, accusing the government of abandoning them to poverty since their release from Albania's Communist jails. The government declared the strike illegal and a judge ordered it halted pending a ruling on its legality."

"Albanians protested nationwide today, despite promises to refund investments made by President Berisha in a speech broadcast on Saturday night on state television." More than a week of angry demonstrations petered out. The opposition Socialist Party charged that President Sali Berisha and his Democratic Party had used the schemes to finance their election campaigns"

"The police fired water cannons and plastic bullets today at thousands of Albanian protesters infuriated by the failure of another pyramid investment scheme that swallowed up their savings. Officers fired into the air from a police van as it cruised along a boulevard of this southern port city, and masked policemen beat up one demonstrator until he lay bloody and motionless on the ground. The police also picked up stones hurled by the protesters and threw them back at the crowd. Many people were hit."

"In Tirana, the capital, police manhandled and beat demonstrators while blocking a rally called by opposition leaders in defiance of a Government ban. The opposition Socialist Party said 15 party leaders had been detained and were later released, but the Government denied that. In Vlore, a southern port, up to 40,000 people took to the streets demanding the return of savings lost after the schemes collapsed this year. The rally was the largest protest of four held there this week. Farther north in Fier, 2,000 demonstrators massed near the city's main square. But the police broke up the rally, attacking protesters and journalists with wooden sticks."

"Anti-Government protesters clashed today with security forces for a fifth consecutive day in the southern port of Vlore, leaving at least 40 people wounded and one man dead of a heart attack, officials said. It was the first death reported since the outbreak of violent protests last month by thousands of Albanians who have lost savings estimated at $1 billion in failed pyramid schemes."

"THE death toll in anti-government riots in the Albanian port of Vlore rose to three yesterday and the Opposition accused the police of opening fire on protesters. One man died of bullet wounds. Hundreds were injured in clashes on the sixth successive day of demonstrations in Vlore, 60 miles south of Tirana, the capital. One man, 48, died on Sunday after he was kicked on the ground in rioting and taken to hospital covered in blood. Police said he had died of a heart attack."

"The police, overwhelmed in riots a day earlier, gave up the streets of this southern port city today to 40,000 angry demonstrators who accuse the officers of murder. The protesters had assembled to bury Artur Rustemi, 30, a store owner, the first victim of a month of rioting over collapsing pyramid schemes, but nobody tried to stop them when they set fire to the ruling Democratic Party headquarters."

"Demonstrations by Albanians angry over failed pyramid investment schemes are stepping up pressure on President Sali Berisha and his Democratic Party. Crowds listened to speeches yesterday in the city of Vlore, where the Mayor and opposition legislators are demanding that the Government resign. (Reuters)"

"Today's protests began with a peaceful demonstration by some 7,000 people on a soccer field outside Tirana."  "Albanian protesters and riot police officers clashed today, with angry crowds hurling stones and the police firing live rounds into the air in the worst violence the capital has seen since widespread unrest erupted last month."  "The police moved in with truncheons and randomly hit protesters, pushing back a crowd of about 1,000 people."  "Albania's Government resigned today after the deadliest violence in two months of angry unrest, but opposition parties and protesters pressed for even more concessions from the embattled President, Sali Berisha."

"Protesters outraged over the killing of an opposition leader set fire to Albania's main government building today and sent the Prime Minister and his Cabinet fleeing in a hail of gunfire. One protester was killed, and four guards of Prime Minister Fatos Nano were wounded as marchers and police officers traded gunfire. Clouds of smoke from burning cars rose over the center of the capital. The violence was set off by the killing of a popular politician, Azem Hajdari, 35, and a bodyguard, who were shot on Saturday in front of headquarters of the opposition Democratic Party."

Protester Group Identity: followers of the former Albanian President Sali Berisha
Notes: "About 3,000 followers of the former Albanian President, Sali Berisha, defied a Government ban and staged a peaceful march today through this capital. " Police in Kosovo have fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters whose rally against EU-backed deals with Serbia and Montenegro ended with them hurling bricks and petrol bombs at government headquarters.  At least 10,000 demonstrators gathered on Saturday in Kosovo's capital, Pristina, to demand the government resign over deals with the fledgling state's neighbours that they claim breach its constitution.  The deals to give Kosovo's Serb minority more rights and to end a border dispute with Montenegro are vital to the state's bid for eventual EU membership, but many Kosovars feel the government bowed to pressure from Brussels and Belgrade.  Officials said 28 people were hurt and about 40 protesters arrested in violence that saw police vehicles and part of government headquarters set ablaze. ""We will not be governed by those who trade our sovereignty. We are seeking free elections to be organised immediately, because they no longer have the right to govern Kosovo,"" said Fatmir Limaj, the leader of one opposition party. A Romanian traffic policeman punished for daring to pull over a politician has become a Facebook hero with more than 260,000 followers - and a bestselling author too - as Romania rises up against its corrupt ruling class. In February, Marian Godina, who regularly posts accounts of his funny or odd encounters with motorists in the town of Brasov, fined the driver of a local councillor for narrowly missing a pedestrian at a crossing. This earned him the wrath of the councillor, who pushed Mr Godina's superiors into accusing him of disrespect and staging a disciplinary inquiry. "In East Germany, head of state Manfred Gerlach told visiting Czech President Vaclav Havel Jan. 3 the Berlin wall will soon be torn down. Former US national security adviser Zbigniew Brzezinski told Polish radio listeners Jan. 3 that Czechoslovakia and Poland should form a federation to protect themselves from the Soviet Union and a reunited Germany. A similar proposal before World War II was rejected. In Bulgaria, about 1,000 demonstrators rallied Jan. 2 outside parliament to protests recent moves to safeguard the rights of the country's Turkish minority."

"Thousands of Soviet Azerbaijanis rioted near the Soviet-Iranian border today, destroying property, harassing Soviet and Iranian border guards and, in some cases, trying to cross illegally into Iran, according to official television and press reports here."  "But Vagiv Samedoglu, a leader of the emerging Azerbaijani Popular Front political movement, disputed the official accounts, saying in a telephone interview that reports of rioting and intoxication in the area were a "monstrous lie and a libel on our people." He said that thousands of ethnic Azerbaijanis had demonstrated peacefully in the region of Nakhichevan along the Iranian frontier to demand an open border between that portion of Soviet Azerbaijan and the Iranian province of Azerbaijan, separated since 1920."

"The Soviet Government reinforced its troops along the Iranian border today in the face of continuing reports of destructive protests by Azerbaijani crowds demanding an open frontier. Soviet officials said angry throngs of thousands of people had destroyed guard towers, crossing alarms and wire fencing along miles of the border, demanding that ancient cultural and political ties between Azerbaijanis on both sides of the Soviet-Iranian border be restored."  "Other accounts by the border guard authorities said the crowd was up to 7,000 and shouted ''down with the Russian empire'' and ''we demand reunification with Iran'' through electronic amplifiers. Some camped in tents, and hundreds of gasoline bombs were thrown at guard posts in the last four days, the authorities said."

"Crowds began tearing down remaining border installations along a stretch of the Soviet frontier with Iran today, but troops patrolling the troubled region in Soviet Azerbaijan did not intervene. Local journalists said the region, Nakhichevan, remained tense after a week of turmoil. The predominantly Shiite Muslim population is demanding more farmland and freer access to Iranian Shiites across the border."
"Meanwhile, 10,000 protesters took to the streets of Baku, the Azerbaijani capital, in sympathy with compatriots in the troubled region."

"Thousands of Lithuanians, shouting and singing their desire for independence, joined a demonstration in the centre of Vilnius yesterday amid signs that Moscow was trying to find at least a temporary solution to the conflict between the Soviet and Lithuanian Communist Party organizations."  "Slogans on the banners they carried ranged from the brazen -- "Gorbachev Go Home and Take the Red Army With You" -- to the aggressive -- "We Didn't Join the Soviet Union, You Grabbed Us" -- as the boisterous crowd of more than 20,000 gathered outside the city cathedral to hear speeches and wave the red, green and yellow flag of prewar independent Lithuania."

"In Soviet Georgia on Thursday, protesters demanding independence for the southern republic drove government workers from their offices in the small town of Kareli, 50 miles northwest of the capital, Tbilisi, according to a telephone report. Irina Sarishvili, a leader of the pro-independence National Democratic Party of Georgia, said by telephone from Tbilisi, the capital, that protesters had occupied the town and regional government offices. A deputy director of Georgia's official press agency, Otar Kapanadze, said he had no information about any disturbances in Kareli. Talks With Moscow Demanded Tbilisi has been the scene of rallies for days by protesters demanding that a Politburo member from Moscow come to negotiate on independence."

"Tass reported that at the Saturday rally in Baku, a crowd of about 130,000 people roared its support for a demand that the republic's Parliament conduct a referendum on withdrawing Azerbaijan from the Soviet Union."  "The journalist, Nazim Ragimov, said the incidents came after some demonstrators broke away from a huge Azerbaijani independence rally after ''provocateurs'' distributed pamphlets calling for a pogrom against Armenians."  "In a new flareup of nationalist unrest, at least two people were killed in the southern city of Baku today during anti-Armenian riots following a huge Azerbaijani independence rally, local journalists said."

"Sporadic fighting broke out again yesterday in Baku as the Azerbaijani parliament met in urgent session to discuss the military clampdown on the city, which has left more than 80 dead and up to 400 wounded. With thousands of weeping and chanting demonstrators defying the state of emergency and gathering outside the republic's Supreme Soviet, deputies denounced the bloodshed and demanded that Moscow withdraw the Army."  "The city council of the embattled capital of Soviet Azerbaijan demanded today that army troops be withdrawn, while thousands of people gathered outside Communist Party headquarters there in defiance of a state of emergency to mourn those killed in this weekend's sudden military occupation."

"Surrounded by thousands of angry Azerbaijanis waving banners saying "Gorbachev hangman" and "Stop the terror in Baku," Gen. Nikolai Smirnov reached for a megaphone. "I can promise you the army did not kill anybody in Baku," he said."  "The scene outside the ministry illustrated the depth of feeling among Azerbaijanis over the military occupation of Baku. But Smirnov's willingness to talk with the demonstrators seemed to reflect an acknowledgment by the Kremlin that the Soviet Union's deep-rooted ethnic problems may require dialogue as well as force."

This is a mass funeral, in which people were protesting against the Soviet intervention and existence of troops in Azerbaijan. "Shortly after the legislature concluded an emergency all-night session, an estimated 1 million people gathered in the city's center for a mass funeral for those killed during the army takeover. Troops withdrew from the streets during the procession with the coffins, and order was maintained by activists of the anti-Communist Azerbaijani Popular Front."

"As the delegates met in Warsaw's Palace of Culture, an intimidating Gothic skyscraper built by the Soviet Union in the 1950's, about 500 youths protested outside, with some of them throwing rocks. The police pushed them away as they yelled ''Down with the Communists!''"

"Throngs of Soviet citizens demonstrated their hunger for democracy today by parading 100,000 strong to the Kremlin walls to demand that the Communist Party surrender its monopoly of power over the life of this troubled nation."  "As the Soviet Communist Party leadership completed preparations for today's crucial Central Committee plenum, an estimated 300,000 people marched through central Moscow yesterday in what was described as one of the biggest street demonstrations since the 1917 Revolution. The marchers condemned the slow pace of reform and demanded the removal of Kremlin conservatives."  "President Gorbachov yesterday bowed to pressure to end the Communist Party's guaranteed right to rule and held out the prospect of a Soviet Union in which the Bolsheviks' heirs would have to compete for power. The concessions were proposed the day after a 300,000-strong demonstration in Moscow showed that the reform movement inside and outside the party was gathering a momentum of its own."

"At least 50,000 people gathered today in the capital of the republic of Moldavia to applaud speakers of both the ruling Communist Party and a radical opposition group as they demanded greater autonomy."

"Defying an emergency decree and a ban on demonstrations, thousands of people rallied Tuesday in the capital of Soviet Tadzhikistan, Soviet television reported early today, saying that as many as 37 people had died since rioting began there late Sunday night. Officials in the city, Dushanbe, appeared Tuesday on local television appealing for calm, and saying that the situation was ''completely out of the control'' of the republic's leadership and the special Soviet troops brought in to help restore order in the Central Asian region." "A crowd of several thousand people gathered in front of Communist Party headquarters in Dushanbe on Tuesday issued an ultimatum with five demands: the expulsion of all Armenian refugees from Tadzhikistan, removal of the Communist Party and government in the republic, closing the Tadzhik aluminum plant in the republic's western region because of environmental dangers, turning over to the people all profits from cotton grown in Tadzhikistan and releasing 25 people who were arrested in disturbances Monday."

"The young Lithuanians at yesterday's protest rally outside the Supreme Soviet in Vilnius yesterday had framed a statement that they intended sending to the Ministry of Defence and the local military commission after they had handed back their notices of conscription. It described the Soviet troops stationed in the Baltic republic as an army of occupation, on the grounds that the Lithuanian Supreme Soviet had declared the republic's annexation to the Soviet Union in 1940 invalid on February 7."

"Tens of thousands of people gathered yesterday in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, to protest living conditions and a lack of consumer goods and medicines, the official Tass news agency reported. The crowd decried ethnic violence in the republic, where rioting in the last week has killed at least 22 people, Tass said."
"Young Moldavians marched through the streets here yesterday demanding that the Soviet ''army of occupation'' should immediately leave their country."

Location of Protest: Moscow, Kiev and in more than 20 other cities
Notes: "The first officially sanctioned mass demonstration by opposition groups in Moscow three weeks ago was almost a celebration of the novelty of demonstrating. The sun shone, there were children and laughter, and the chief targets of the marchers' placards were hardliners in the leadership. Yesterday's pre-election demonstration, in contrast, was a serious political event which brought several hundred thousand people together in a concerted protest against Communist Party rule."  "Radical political groups demanding a faster transition to democracy staged demonstrations across the Soviet Union today, drawing thousands of protesters who brushed aside official warnings of possible violence. Between 50,000 and 100,000 people gathered in central Moscow to call on Communist authorities to begin an East European-style dialogue with independent social organizations and support reformist candidates in local elections. Smaller demonstrations took place in other Soviet cities, from the Ukrainian capital of Kiev in the west to Vladivostok in the far east."

"The police arrested 31 people today at an unauthorized demonstration in which protesters shouted anti-Communist slogans, the official news agency Tass reported. The news agency said that several hundred people gathered in downtown Moscow at a protest gathered by the Democratic Union, an unofficial political party, to commemorate the 1917 revolution that ended czarist rule."

Protester Group Identity: radiation victims of the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear acciden
Notes: "More than 100 radiation victims of the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear accident are on a hunger strike to protest inadequate medical care, including shortages of drugs and hospital beds, the Tass news agency said. The news agency, quoting a report in the labor daily Trud, said about 120 people were fasting at the Institute of Medical Radiology as of Wednesday. The institute is in the Ukrainian city of Kharkov, 400 miles southwest of Moscow. Tass did not say when the strike began."

"TENS of thousands of Ukrainians defied the authorities on Saturday and held mass meetings throughout the Ukraine in support of Lithuanian independence. The action, called by Rukh, the Ukrainian nationalist movement, was the biggest demonstration of solidarity with Lithuania so far inside the Soviet Union. In the Ukrainian capital, Kiev, an estimated 30,000 demonstrators passed a resolution criticizing President Gorbachov for ''interfering in the internal affairs of the independent Lithuanian republic'' and urging him to ''withdraw the occupying troops'' from Lithuania."

"Lithuanian President Vytautas Landsbergis told a cheering crowd, estimated at about 300,000 people, that Lithuania would not rescind its March 11 declaration of independence, despite intense pressure from the Kremlin. "Iron will melt to wax, and water will turn to stone, before we will retreat," he said, repeating the battle cry of Lithuania's 14th-century national hero, Duke Gediminas."

"Soviet Georgians gathered to protest on the first anniversary of the Kremlin's crackdown against peaceful demonstrators. The tens of thousands in opposition lack the organization of secessionists in other republics."  "HUNDREDS of thousands of Georgian protesters marched on the Soviet Army's Transcaucasian military headquarters yesterday afternoon to demand its withdrawal from this Soviet republic and allow it to declare its independence from Moscow."

"Tens of thouands of people attended an open-air service in Kiev today and workers in the Byelorussian city of Gomel went on strike as the Soviet Union marked the fourth anniversary of the Chernobyl nuclear disaster. A crowd estimated at 60,000 people waving nationalist flags packed the square in front of Sofia Cathedral in Kiev, the Ukrainian capital, and listened to calls to punish all those responsible for the world's worst nuclear accident, witnesses said."

"Waving their fists and jeering the Kremlin leadership, tens of thousands of Muscovites today transformed the traditional May Day celebration of "socialist labor" on Red Square into a caustic rebuke of Communist power. Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev seemed transfixed at times as the parade, once a tightly controlled ritual of hollow hurrahs, suddenly became a boisterous demonstration of popular anger and protest. Some demonstrators carried Lithuanian and Czarist-era Russian flags, and a few even displayed Soviet flags with the hammer and sickle torn out."

Protester Group Identity: the Green Party and New Forum
Notes: "Upset that the Soviet commander declared himself unauthorized to limit training flights, activists from the Green Party and New Forum organized a demonstration against the base May 21 that drew 6,000 to 8,000 protesters. It was the third such demonstration aimed at the Soviet military since the Berlin Wall was breached last November. Meanwhile, a petition for removal of the base garnered more than 8,000 signatures, the mayor said."

This demonstration is a part of massive strikes throughout the Soviet Union.
