The nurses however returned to the mortuary ahead of the mourners and barricaded its entrance. Officer from Mbale police station dispersed the crowds..."
Exact date is unclear. "In March, residents held peaceful demonstrations demanding Nkoyo's removal, claiming he was incompetent. The residents were led by 20 MCAsÃ¢ÂÂ¦"

1) "Hundreds of Taveta squatters went on hunger strike on Tuesday, in protest against alleged land injustices by the area's government officers. The hunger strike began with a demonstration from Taveta Sisal area to the subcounty commissioner's office where they spent the night. The squatters complained that many of them were not allocated portions of 15,000 acres of land the government bought to settle them...The squatters further demanded the immediate release of the subcounty's land rights activists arrested and charged last week..."; 2) "HUNDREDS of squatters in Taita Taveta are on a hunger strike to protest land injustices by government officers. The squatters want the immediate release of land rights activists from Taveta who were arrested two weeks ago and charged at the Voi law courts. The hunger strike began on Tuesday with a protest march from Taveta sisal area to the town..."

"PARENTS and pupils of Thessalia Primary School on the Kisumu and Kericho border are opposed to privatising the school. More than 350 pupils held demonstrations on Tuesday. The parents say an administrator of Thessalia Mission Clement Oguta has turned part of the primary school into a private secondary school. They urged President Uhuru Kenyatta and Education Cabinet Secretary Jacob Kaimenyi to intervene. Parents said Oguta did not consult the community."

"Residents of Wamunyu market demonstrated on the Machakos-Kitui road on Saturday. They said about 30 lorries ferry sand from Athi River every night. The protesters blocked the road with stones, causing a traffic snarl-up. Hundreds of youth engaged the police in running battles, forcing the officers to teargas and disperse them. Youth leader Shadrack Mutuku said their continued complaints to the authorities and the county government always landed on deaf years. He said too much scooping may weaken the Athi River Bridge's foundation. "Some of those doing this business are well-connected in the county government," Mutuku said."

"Nairobi Road Primary School parents want the government to stop the grabbing of a section of the school's land. More than 300 parents held a peaceful demonstration at the school on Monday. They urged the government to revoke the titles of nine plots already issued to individuals."

1) "The Kilifi government yesterday agreed to reduce the taxes. An elderly woman was killed on Monday during a demonstration of thousands of traders demonstrated against the increased rates. Police have denied killing the woman, saying they did not use live bullet to disperse the demonstrators. Governor Amason Kingi intervened to stop the demo and promised the the traders the County Finance Act will be amended to reduce the levies..."; 2) "A human rights organisation wants the commanders of police units who led the operation to disperse traders during demonstration in Malindi last Monday to be suspended. An elderly woman was killed. Haki Africa said the senior officials should be suspended pending investigations as they were responsible for the use of live bullets, one of which killed Mbodze Makupe..."

"RESIDENTS of Sabatia constituency on Monday burned two shops and a house over the release on bond of two murder suspects. The hundreds of villagers from Vokoli also blocked Eldoret-Chavakali road for hours and injured one police officer. They were protesting against the release on Sunday of Joyce Imungu and Emily Muhonja. The two had been arrested on Friday in connection with the death of Edith Jadenya, 46...On Monday morning, police were forced to shoot in the air to disperse the villagers, who wanted to lynch Muhonja Chaos erupted when police were called to rescue Muhonja from the crowd..."

"A man shot dead by police was buried yesterday in Mukurweini township after a battle between the cops and residents. King'ori Kanyi, 33, had a misunderstanding with policemen at a local pub. On March 7, two officers came for him at his house and shot him dead in the family coffee farm at night. Yesterday morning, 500 mourners stormed the Mukurweini police station and dumped a coffin in the compound. Mourners camped outside the police station, demanding that the officers who killed King'ori take the body for burial 500m away. Mukurweini politician Dick Wathika arrived at the scene after a one-hour stand off...Police fired in the air to disperse the crowd but the mourners pelted officers with stones. One officer was seriously injured in the melee with gunshots renting the air...Police later found themselves on the receiving end when they threw teargas unto the mourners who were leaving station only for the teargas to turn against them..."

Unclear if the previous protest on Thursday should be coded, no indication of size. "Activists under the banner Okoa Dada Kenya on Tuesday marched from Freedom Corner in Nairobi to Parliament Building calling on the government to deal with the rise in sexual violence in the country. The march follows a similar protest by activists and members of the civil society on Thursday. In a statement read on behalf of the group by activist Diana Okello, Okoa Dada said rape cases have dominated recent news reports saying that mind-sets need to change now to assure women and girls of their safety..."President Uhuru Kenyatta, this is also corruption," the group added. Okoa Dada Kenya further appealed to the judiciary to handle rape cases seriously and empathize with survivors...The group also called on Women MPs to take action against sexual violence..."

"MORE than 5,000 Kikuyu and Kabete constituency traders have pledged not to pay increased fees. Many staged a peaceful protest yesterday against the controversial Kiambu Finance Bill, which raised licence fees. They said Governor William Kabogo is not within the law to change fees for different licenses by word of mouth..."

"Kenyan university students marched in the capital on Tuesday to demand more security from the government after gunmen killed nearly 150 people at a campus in the eastern town of Garissa last weekÃ¢ÂÂ¦On Tuesday, hundreds of students from different universities walked through the streets in the city singing and shouting, and some headed to the office of the president where they presented a petition."

"More than 100 Kenya Medical Training College workers have downed their tools to demand implementation of collective bargaining agreement signed in 2012. On Tuesday, the workers staged a peaceful demonstration outside KMTC Nakuru campus paralysing operations in the institution..."

Exact date is unclear. "Kisii Governor James Ongwae has warned residents against politicising the provisions in the county's Finance Act. Last week, a group of people marched through the town streets protesting against increased license fees. Ongwae asked those aggrieved to follow the right procedures to have their issue addressed."

"THREE Kiambu MPs on Wednesday led hundreds of traders in Thika town to protest against increased taxes by the county government. Led by Kiambu MPs Alice Ng'ang'a (Thika Town), Jude Njomo (Kiambu Town) and Kimani Ichung'wa (Kikuyu), the traders demanded the resignation of Governor William Kabogo. They had gone to present a memorandum of amendments in his office but Kabogo was in Kiambu launching an E-system..."

1) "THOUSANDS of travellers were yesterday left stranded after the Eldoret-Kisumu highway was barricaded by boda boda operators. The operators in Mosoriot, Nandi county, lit a bonfire to protest against a police crackdown. Thirty motorcycles were seized and 20 people arrested during the crackdown. Among those arrested included AIC pastor Dickson Leting, whose motorcycle was impounded outside a hotel. He was arrested for protesting after his motorcycle was loaded onto a waiting lorry. For nine hours, the highway remained a no-go zone as residents joined the protest and threatened to burn vehicles that defied their orders to stop. Former MP Mark Too negotiated with the traffic police to release the boda boda operators and their motorcycles, which had been taken to Kapsabet police headquarters."; 2) "Officers lobbed teargas canisters when the operators marched to the Machakos police station to demand the release of colleagues arrested during the demonstration."

"A group of meat traders and slaughterhouse workers in Mukurwe-ini, Nyeri, have accused the county government of perpetrating corruption and nepotism in the rehabilitation of the county abattoir. The more than 100 traders held a demonstration in Sunday ion Gakindu town over the delay in rehabilitating the slaughterhouse. They said the slaughterhouse, which was closed down by public health officers three years ago, is yet to be rehabilitated because of an "unprofessional and flawed" tendering process..."

"Mandera County Referral Hospital has been closed following a health workers' strike for higher salaries. More than 459 health workers chanted 'haki yetu' along streets and waved placards with their demands in a demonstration on Monday afternoon. They want their salaries increased from Sh58,000 in group H to Sh65,000 in group K...Six Kenya National Union of Nurses officials were arrested for allegedly inciting the health workers to strike. They spent Monday night in jail after they were denied bail following an alleged call from a county government official, but were released on Tuesday morning."

Protester Group Identity: residents, Kenya National Union of Teachers
Notes: "Business was brought to a standstill in Marigat town on Monday after hundred of residents demonstrates over insecurity in Baringo county. The residents want the government to find a lasting solution to the perennial insecurity taking a toll on the county's development since 2002. They pointed an accusing finger at President Uhuru Kenyatta, his Deputy President William Ruto, and Interior Cabinet Secretary Joseph Nkaissery for doing little to arrest the problem...Led by the Kenya National Union of Teachers Baringo branch Executive Secretary Charles Kamuren, the residents said over 38,000 students are out of school this term due to insecurity. The demonstrators matched through the streets the town carrying placards with the writings; "Government we want to go back home. Over 183 people have been killed in Baringo county. We are being finished by cattle rustlers. President Obama come and safe Kenya."..."

"Tuk-Tuk operators and taxi drivers yesterday protested against harassment by Machakos county officers. Led by their chairman, Joseph Mutisya, the motorists who operate in Machakos town and its environs blocked sections of the town as they marched to the Machakos police station, demanding fair treatment. Speaking to the press, Mutisya said the mistreatment has been escalating. "I have been receiving complaints from the operators that the county officers are harassing them demanding money yet we pay tax just like other businesspeople," he said."

"GOVERNOR Hassan Joho showed disrespect when he sent county executives to meet Nyali MP Hezron Awiti, the legislator said yesterday. Awiti went to Joho's office in Kizingo on Wednesday to discuss revenue collection, education and health in his constituency. However, Joho sent chief of staff Idris Abdulrahman and county executives Francis Thoya (Lands) and Tendai Mtana (Education). "I couldn't table my constituents' grievances for I felt it was disrespectful for the governor to delegate his duties," Awiti told the Star yesterday. The MP, who was accompanied by MCAs Mohamed Ndanda and Jabess Oduor and hundreds of his supporters, stormed out of the meeting in protest. He led a peaceful demonstration, marching from Joho's offices to Furaha Plaza on Nkrumah Road. However, Thoya, Tendai and Abdulrahman said Awiti's letter was clear that he wanted to meet the county executives..."

"A youth is admitted at the Coast General Hospital after he was shot on Saturday evening during a forced eviction in Utange village, Kisauni. Ronal Baya was shot in the leg after residents of Utange resisted evictions. More protests were witnessed yesterday morning as hundreds of residents demanded justice. Residents said Baya was shot as he tried to run away from the police who he thought were thugs. The residents blocked Utange road and lit bonfires as they chanted anti-oppression songs. Kisauni police boss Richard Ngatia could not be reached for comment as calls to his phone did not go through..."

"Women in Makueni county on Tuesday held a peaceful demonstration to oppose a bill on the implementation of the two-thirds gender rule. Among them were county women's representative Rose Museo, Kibwezi East MP Jessica Mbalu and Deputy Governor Adelina Mwau. There was a huge traffic snarl-up on the road towards the county headquarters in Wote town. The more than 50 women accused National Assembly Speaker Justin Muturi of giving his views on the matter yet he "is the CEO of the House". They said he should be neutral. "We want Muturi to stop thinking for us. We all have equal rights and you should actually Respect the constitution, Period," a placard read. Mwau held a meeting with the group at Kusyombunguo Resort. Those present said they support the Kenya Women Parliamentarians. Mwau said the proposal to implement the gender rule progressively should be put on hold."

"More than 2,000 people in Garba Tulla subcounty yesterday protested against the alleged kidnapping of three people by the Kenya Wildlife Service rangers. They were backed by Isiolo Governor Godana Doyo and Isiolo South MP Abdulah Banticha who yesterday said they have asked the government to investigate. Residents said Adan Ismael, Halake Kalicha and Godana Guyo went missing two days ago. They had been tracked and abducted by the rangers along Duse-Bibi-Kinna road residents said..."

Protester Group Identity: Gusii Institute of Technology students, youth
Notes: 1) "Seven people were injured in a clash between the police and students of Gusii Institute of Technology who were protesting the death of two of their classmates. The two were hit by a lorry allegedly being driven by a police officer at Daraja Moja area along Kisii-Keroka Highway on Thursday night. It is said that the officer was driving the vehicle to a Kisii Police Station after seizing it from a driver flouting traffic rules at Kegati area. The demonstrators denied the police access to the scene where the two bodies lay under electricity poles, said Kisii County Police Commander Simeon Kiragu. They burned the lorry and used some of the poles to block the road, and hurled stones at motorists paralysing transport, Kiragu said. They torched eight vehicles at a nearby police station, he said, adding that police patrols have been intensified. Kiragu said two police officers sustained injuries as the students engaged them in running battles. The other casualties were three students and two members of the public, he said..."; 2) "Two pedestrians said to be employees of the institute were hit by a lorry transporting electricity poles last Thursday evening. The driver was a traffic police officer. Students from the institute started rioting and were joined by youths. Eight cars were set ablaze and a petrol station vandalised on Friday..."

"Anti-riot police in Lamu on Sunday morning dispersed a demonstration against Governor Issa Timamy's move to revoke land ownership in the Manda area. Security has been beefed up following the demo threatsÃ¢ÂÂ¦"

"One person was killed and 11 others sustained bullet wounds when Kenya Wildlife Service rangers and residents in Isiolo clashed at Kinna adjacent to Meru National park on Monday. Hundreds of residents took to the street protesting against the disappearance of the three people last week, accusing the KWS of kidnapping them. The residents marched to the Meru National Park and allegedly set a fire at the park. However locals claimed that it was KWS who set the park on fire...Isiolo County Commissioner Wanyama Musiambo confirmed the incident and warned that action will be taken against those behind the shooting. Isiolo Governor Godana Doyo said he regretted that the peaceful protest turned violent. He asked the national government to investigate and arrest the officers behind the shooting...Locals staged demonstrations and blocked the roads leading to Meru and Garba-Tulla demanding KWS vacate the Meru National park. They asked President Uhuru Kenyatta to intervene and relocate the park to avoid further conflict."

"Transport on Moi South Lake road in Naivasha was paralysed for more than three hours as residents protested the closure of a public corridor leading to Lake Naivasha. The more than 400 residents blocked the road using boulders and light fires to protest the closure demanded justice. They were dispersed by the anti-riot police from Nakuru. Landing Beach Association chair David Kilo said the closure has led to job losses for the fish traders. Kilo said the land supports many families. He said a private developer claiming ownership of the land is using senior government officers to oppress them..."

Second day of protests that began on May 27. 1) "A bus belonging to a flower farm was set on fire and scores injured after protests over the closure of the corridor leading to Lake Naivasha entered its second day. Residents of Karagita estate, Naivasha engaged police in running battles on Thursday. Hundreds of flower farm workers, international tourists and motorists were caught up in the demonstration that left scores nursing various injuries. National Land Commission chair Mohammed Swazuri, who toured the closed corridor promised that the issue would be resolved in one week...The sentiments were echoed by Hellsgate MCA Jonathan Warothe who challenged the governor to take charge and direct that the corridor be opened up. The emotional MCA said that tens of people had been injured during the two day riots and hundreds of others left homeless. The clashes which started on Wednesday erupted after police acting on a court orders closed down the corridor which leads to Karagita landing beach. The move angered hundreds of residents in Karagita estate who rely on the lake for fishing. The residents on a rampage blocking the busy Moi South Lake road and stoning motorists. Later in the day, hired goons razed down all structures on the landing beach fueling the demonstrators' anger. They reacted by damaging property belonging nearby flower farm."; 2) "A flower farm bus was torched and scores of people left nursing bullets wounds as the public corridor closure Naivasha protests entered day two..."

"Hundreds of residents of Ngenia village in Laikipia North constituency yesterday demonstrated over poor state of roads in the area. They planted vegetation on the Kwa Makara- Umande road, accusing area Member of Parliament Mathew Lempurkel and the county government of neglecting them...They urged the MP to consider repairing the road by putting murram so that transport can be eased..."

"YOUTH employed to repair roads at Jomvu in Mikindani, Mombasa county, held a protest march on Monday over delayed pay. Each of them wants to be paid Sh8,400 in arrears. The workers said they were forced to strike after their efforts to reach their MP Badi Twalib to listen to their complaints hit a snag..."

"The Nakuru government on Wednesday closed down 50 businesses at Kabatini trading centre in Subukia due to lack of pit latrines. The public health office issued a notice on Tuesday warning that should the business owners fail to comply with the notice, they risk being prosecuted for violating the Public Health Act. The notice was copied to the area OCS, subcounty AP commander and the divisional public health officer. On Wednesday, the business owners held a protest march in the town and accused the county government of double standards as they have already paid for single business permits. "The Nakuru government is to blame for failing to provide public toilets," said John Munyiri who operates an electronics shop..."

1) "Human Rights activist Boniface Mwangi has been arrested and allegedly beaten after he filmed the protest between boda boda operators in the CBD and city council officers on Wednesday morning. Mwangi was arrested by AP officers guarding City Hall before he was handed over to the Nairobi Central police station for questioning. Police said he was arrested for obstruction, causing chaos, mobilising boda boda riders to demonstrate in town and engaging city county askaris in running battle. He was also accused of causing a major CBD traffic snarl up. The riders stormed central police and engaged the police in running battles in their protest against alleged harassment by city council officers. Police are yet to release Mwangi despite pressure from city activists..."; 2) "Hundreds of boda boda operators yesterday held a demonstration outside City Hall in Nairobi, accusing city askaris of harassment. The operators were from the CBD, Eastleigh, Dandora, Mathare, Kayole, Bahati and Kariobangi. They accused the askaris of arresting and extorting money from them..."

"Police and the residents of Engineer trading centre in Nyandarua county clashed over a haul of illicit brew stored in a police station on Saturday. The residents wanted to destroy the samples the police had confiscated from a bar 50 metres away. The police blocked the residents led by Nyandarua county women's representative Wanjiku Muhia from destroying the 1,200 cartons of liquor. The angry residents stormed the police station demanding to know why samples of the brew were being stored in the station instead of being destroyed. Muhia went to seek audience with the deputy police boss Peterson Gitaga but she was turned away in full glare of TV cameras. Police lobbed teargas at the crowd accompanying the MP when they asked to know why she was not being listened to. The residents who barricaded the Miharati- Njabini road as police in riot gear engaged them in running battles. Several people including a police officer sustained minor injuries in the five-hour melee. The protesters hurled stones at the riot police who shot in the air to disperse the crowd. Muhia accused the police of protecting traders in the illicit brew business."

"The University of Eldoret was shut down indefinitely on Wednesday following student riots over fee increments. Vice Chancellor Teresia Akenga ordered students to leave by 2pm saying property of unknown value was destroyed during the protest. Anti-riot police were deployed to the university where students hurled stones at buildings and vehicles..."

"THE Kakamega administration has promised to evict traders from the CBD. Head of Communication Sumba Juma yesterday said all traders have been allocated stalls at the county main market. Juma accused the traders of politicising their relocation even though they were given an eviction notice. Administration police and county askaris engaged traders in running battles in Kakamega town on Thursday. Some traders said they are yet to be given an alternative stall. Three traders and Mahiakalo MCA Cleophas Malala were arrested during the riot and locked up in Kakamega police station for several hours..."

"Manunga Girls Secondary School in Kipipiri, Nyandarua county, has been closed indefinitely after students went on the rampage. The 300 students stormed out of the school on Monday night and spent the night on the Ol Kalou-Miharati road. They were protesting against what they termed harshness by the management. The students want the principal and her deputy transferred. Kipipiri police boss Murkomen Chebet said the students stormed out at 10pm. Chebet said the students complained of being given small food rations. "They also accused the school management of denying them permission to go with food to their hostels," he said."

"Residents of Shanzu ward, Mombasa county, yesterday protested against the area MCA for not stopping land grabbing. They braved the rain and marched to the Bamburi police station, threatening to recall MCA Maimuna Salim. "We are tired of having our lands grabbed," resident Athman Mwajazi said..."

Protester Group Identity: female administrative police, Kenya Association of Women in Policing
Notes: "Female APs took to the streets of Kakamega town on Monday, in a protest against elections from which their representative was allegedly barred. The officers, under the Kenya Association of Women in Policing, claimed Maureen Lidava, who sought to represent the Nyanza/ Western region was wrongfully locked out. Following the countrywide poll, largely boycotted in Western and Nairobi, they marched across the town in their uniforms, waving placards saying 'No Maureen, No Voting', 'No Lidava, No Voting'. But officials of the election held earlier in the day, and tallied at Police Pavilion in Nairobi, said Lidava did not meet the deadline for submitting papers..."

"Siaya county workers stormed Governor Cornel Rasanga's office demanding their rights, as part of a protest that began at midnight. The workers, including those from the health sector, earlier marched through the town chanting "no pay, no work", and gathered at the Siaya County Referral Hospital. The health sector, which has the largest number of workers, is most affected. "We have not been paid last month's salaries. There are arrears and the state of our facilities is deplorable," a protester said...The protester said when they got to the governor's office, they were informed that their money had been sent to the wrong account..."

"RESIDENTS of Garissa town yesterday took to the streets demanding a solution to deteriorating education standards in Northeastern. More than 800 teachers have fled the region after terror attacks in Mandera and Garissa. Led by 47 civil society groups, the residents waved placards and marched from Garissa Primary School to the regional coordinator's offices. Parents, schoolchildren and other education players took part in the March. They handed Northeastern regional coordinator Mohamud Saleh a memo for President Uhuru Kenya. "We all know why the teachers and health personnel left this region," Saleh told them. "As residents we should denounce terrorism." The coordinator blamed insecurity on internal conflicts and urged the residents to "re-examine themselves"..."

Protester Group Identity: residents, lobbyists, Kisumu City Residents Voice, Kisumu Youth Caucus, MCAs
Notes: "ABOUT 1,000 residents and lobbyists in Kisumu town yesterday held a demonstration in protest against worsening insecurity...Carrying twigs, placards and banners, the protesters marched from Taifa Park on Oginga Odinga Street to Kenyatta Avenue. They chanted anti-police slogans and songs outside Central police station. Armed officers formed a cordon at the entrance to keep them off. The protestors were led by Ogada, Kisumu Youth Caucus officials Erick Okello and Dennis Menya and MCAs Edwine Anayo and Paul Achayo. Ogada read a petition citing measures they want taken to stop crime...The residents demanded a county policing authority be formed."

"Some 600 farmers from Karangi village in Kiganjo ward, Gatundu South, have opposed a mega dam. The National Irrigation Board plans to build the dam to irrigate 37 sublocations on the farmers' 27 acres. During a demonstration on Monday, spokesman Joseph Njoroge said they were not consulted by the government or the irrigation board. Njoroge said the dam should be constructed in the Kinale Forest, instead of displacing the 600 inhabitants. Farmers' Committee member Gabriel Kamau accused NIB officials and the provincial administration of intimidation..."

"More than 300 striking nurses in Nyeri town blocked four cash couriers during a protest that saw them sleep on a road on Tuesday. They had camped outside Governor Nderitu Gacagua's office seeking to talk to him, when the vehicles approached with their sirens on. The protesters were forced out of the way after about five minutes, during which six AP officers stepped out of the vehicles and cocked their guns...Waving twigs and placards, the health workers, most of whom were female nurses, shouted at them after they passed. Gacagua did not turn up to address the group that police tried in vain to control. The health workers earlier protested within the town before heading to the office of county Health executive Charles Githinji, where they were turned away by police. Githinji has insisted that the strike, which began last Monday, is illegal saying the Kenya National Union of Nurses has received a court order stopping it. But Nyeri KNUN chairperson Ann Nyawira has maintained that the strike, which has led to the crowding to private hospitals, will continue..."

"Only unapproved buildings are being targeted in the ongoing demolitions in Kiambu, a county official has said. Ten buildings were demolished in Juja estate on Saturday. Residents on Saturday were woken up by earth-movers pulling down the houses. Police provided security to prevent any chaos. Officers lobbed tear-gas canisters at residents protesting against the demolition. Several people were injured and rushed to hospital..."

"Despite earlier threats from the county government to sack them, the striking workers demonstration was joined by residents and Nyeri Town MP Esther Murugi on Monday. They camped outside the Health executive Charles Githinji's office for hours, demanding to speak to Governor Nderitu Gachagua. He did not speak to them. The protesters also burnt effigies of Githinji and his chief officer Peter Munyua..."

"Hundreds of residents from Kishushe and Paranga locations on Tuesday held peaceful demonstrations to protest against land problems. They marched to Taita Taveta Governor John Mruttu's office and handed their petition to Deputy Governor Mary NdighaÃ¢ÂÂ¦"

Protester Group Identity: residents, youth,  JAP Nyeri branch, The Citizen Initiative
Notes: "More than 500 Nyeri county residents held an 'Operation Rudisha Health Services to National Government' on Thursday. Waving twigs and placards in a march around town on Thursday, they criticised the county for failing to end the nurse's strike that is in its third week. They lit bonfires and camped outside Governor Nderitu Gachagua's office demanding to present him a petition. The protesters, who prevented entry into the office, were joined by JAP Nyeri branch chairman Wambugu Nyamu, coordinator Samson Kagiri and officials of The Citizen Initiative. A group of youths forced its way into the offices before Nyeri OCS Raphael Gaa arrived with a contingent of police officers. The youths banged the gate, lay on the road and chanted slogans against the governor, amid pleas by the officers for them to calm down..."

"Hundreds of youths stormed a slaughterhouse in Bungoma county for a look at 10 wheelbarrows bought at Sh109,000 each by the Agriculture ministry. Waving pacards and twigs, the youths, majority of whom were juakali craftsmen, demonstrated against the purchase, which has raised concerns of fraud by county executives. "We as juakali artsians have looked at those wheelbarrows; they can't cost more than Sh3,000," said their chairman Moses Wekesa. The demonstrators, who disrupted business with marches on Bungoma town's main streets, said the protests will only end once action is taken. The marched to Governor Kenneth Lusaka's office demanding to speak with him. It took the intervention County Assembly Majority leader Majimbo Okumu for them to calm down...

"Teachers in several counties demonstrated on Monday over their salary increase stalemate, ignoring a TSC sack threat over their strike. The strike over a 50 to 60 per cent pay hike, upheld by the Supreme Court, has entered its second week...Knut secretary general Wilson Sossion addressed the teachers outside the union's headquarters during the Nairobi demo that Kuppet officials also joined...In Kisumu, the teachers stormed the county headquarters after holding a peaceful demonstration in town, and demanded to speak with Governor Jack Ranguma. They waved placards criticising Kaimenyi and SRC chairperson Sarah Serem, and demanded that the court ruling be honoured. The TSC had asked teachers to report to work today, saying those on strike would be "deemed to have absconded duty and removed from the payroll with immediate effect."..."

"COUNTY health workers in Nairobi downed their tools yesterday citing discrimination, late salaries and poor working conditions. They issued the strike notice on August 20. The worst-affected hospitals are Mama Lucy Kibaki and Mbagathi, whose staff camped in protest at Uhuru Park..."

"Most public schools in Eldoret town remained shut yesterday as teachers protested in the streets. They urged President Uhuru and Deputy President William Ruto to resolve the standoff. The teachers said the President should speak about the pay dispute. But teachers in private schools were at work."

"Kenya National Union of Teachers Murang'a South branch members yesterday took to the streets asking for their court-ordered pay increase from the Teachers Service Commission. The teachers led by their branch secretary Amos Murigi, chairman John Njata, Murang'a woman representative Mary Kimani and other executives protested around Kenol market. The teachers said they will not report to work, even if they are served with sacking letters. They said TSC chairpaerson Lydia Nzomo and executive secretary Nancy Macharia should be charged with contempt of court..."

"NYS employees took to the streets on Monday protesting over delayed payments by the Devolution ministry. They marched from South B to CS Anne Waiguru's office at Harambee House carrying placards written "We are being eaten by vultures, Waiguru must go" and "Show them we can make it without them". "We have not been paid for eight weeks by the ministry, we cannot be working for them and they do not appreciate our efforts. This is tiring," said one of the protesters. The youth from Mukuru Kayaba said more than 2,000 were sacked without warning, claiming some were misled into taking leave, but did not get their jobs back upon return..."

"Gender activists accused the police and the Judiciary of handling rape cases slowly during a demonstration against sexual violence in the Nairobi CBD on Monday. The marched on streets, further accusing the government of "taking very little action", and demanding justice against a 'gynaecologist' accused of rape...The demonstrators further marched to the offices of the CJ, the IG and the DPP to deliver their petitions..."

"EMBU Governor Martin Wambora has told unemployed youth his government will address their plight...The youth wielded placards before gathering at the county government headquarters in Embu...He said plans are underway to open more factories to provide more jobs. Wambora said his government has sponsored youth who travelled to Dubai and Qatar for employment. The youth said the government only makes empty promises, which are never implemented. The group blew whistles and vuvuzelas and chanted "Wambora sio bora" (Wambora is not the best). They were joined by boda boda riders. The youth demonstrators said they are yet to get contracts and funds from the county government. They said only well-connected youth get government benefits. The youth lit a bonfire at the county headquarters using waste papers, demanding to be allowed in. They said the county government has not set aside enough funds to empower them through their talents."

"A group of civil societies in Nairobi yesterday protested against lifting the ban on genetically modified foods, saying they are unsafe for consumption. The protesters marched from Freedom Corner to Deputy President William Ruto's office in the CBD, where they presented a petition for the ban not to be lifted. This comes after Ruto last month said the government is planning to lift the ban on GMOs in two months..."

"More than 200 residents of Tetu, Nyeri county, protested against Cord leader Raila Odinga's "regular attacks" on Devolution CS Ann Waiguru on Thursday. The protesters said Raila should not taint Waiguru's name over the Sh791 million NYS scandal, and asked him to respect women instead of fighting them...The protesters lay on Giakanja-Gathuthi highway blocking it, before marching to Wamagana trading centre waving twigs and placards. Area police boss Stephen Obara stopped the demonstration for an address by Deputy county commissioner Herman Shambi. Shambi assured the youths that the programme, which had been put off, would resume and their arrears paid this week."

1) "At least 10 students were arrested and taken to Central police station amid running battles with police in a demonstration over delayed Helb loans on Tuesday. Police used tear gas to disperse the students, who stepped on 'Kidero grass' and harassed motorists in a march Uhuru Highway in the Nairobi CBD. "We want our money! Comrades-power," they chanted as they marched to Treasury offices, causing traffic and forcing motorists to use alternative routes..."; 2) "Twenty University of Nairobi students were arrested yesterday during a protest in the city centre to demand quick approval of Helb loans. They engaged the police in street battles which lasted for hours. At least 20 students were arrested and taken to the Central police station. Police lobbed teargas canisters to disperse the students who were throwing stones. Sonu chairman Babu Owino, who led the demonstration, accused the Finance ministry of frustrating students by delaying the money..."

"Scores of demonstrators were yesterday injured and others arrested as police dispersed a demonstration in Kisumu town. The demonstrators were marching towards the Kisumu government offices to protest against rising crime. Residents want Governor Jack Ranguma to form the County Policing Authority...They said people are being killed daily but the governor does not want to listen to their grievances. The demonstrators said the county government is not doing its part to fight crime. Police officers confiscated boda boda motorcycles left behind by fleeing demonstrators...The students started the march from their hostels to the Helb offices at the Anniversary Towers, then to the National Treasury through Uhuru Highway and Harambee Avenue. They went back to campus through Tom Mboya Street and University Way where they clashed with police..."

"About 200 parents from St Catherine Primary School in South B, Nairobi have marched to Ardhi House to protest against the grabbing of the school's playground. The parents walked the 5kms to Lands CS Charity Ngilu's office on Wednesday, carrying placards with anti-land grabbing messages..."

1) "Maseno University's administration block was burnt on Wednesday night by student arsonists and rioters angry they were barred from contesting elections...A senior police officer told the Star rioting students lit bonfires before attacking security guards at the main entrance, forcing them to flee...Sources in the university said the fire is linked to elections of Student Organisation of Maseno University...The sources said some of the candidates barred from contesting might have started the fire. The candidates were blocked after they failed to meet the election requirements..."

"In the town on Monday, more than 200 commercial sex workers protested against poor security saying many of their colleagues are killed by men pausing as clinets. Spokesperson Daisy Achieng said they should be protected as they make significant contributions to the economy."

1) "Residents of Kabete constituency yesterday held demonstrations over poor roads and accused MP Ferdinand Waititu of not fixing them. They blocked the Wangige-Rwaka road at Gikuni using stones, logs and lit bonfires using old tyres. This resulted in a traffic snarl-up for hours. They said Waititu promised to tarmac the Wangige-Gikuni road during his campaigns, but it has gotten worse...Officers from Waititu's office, led by Simon Ngugi, arrived tried without success to stop the demonstrations...The demonstrators were later dispersed by officers from Kikuyu police station, led by OCS Joshua Arende..."; 2) "The residents on Monday closed the Wangige-Rwaka road at Gikuni, causing a traffic snarl-up for most of the day. They accused Waititu of lying to them during the campaigns that the Ruku-Ngecha, Mukui-Nyathuna and Gikuni-Wangige roads would be tarmacked once he was elected. The protesters, led by a group calling itself the Cuba Elites, said Waititu is never seen in Kabete, but only heard in the press criticizing Governor William Kabogo or playing politics..."

1) "The Technical University of Mombasa was closed indefinitely on Monday after students took to the streets in protest against fee increment..They blocked roads around the institution in Tudor area, KRCS said via Twitter, and set two county lorries on fire, preventing access on Bakhstan road. Police lobbed teargas canisters and fired in the air as the students engaged them in running battles. The students accused the university of increasing the school fees by Sh3,000 without "official communication". "This fee also varies from one department to the other. In some classes it has been increased from Sh6,000 to Sh8,000," one said..."; 2) "Students rioted yesterday over increased fees at the Technical University of Mombasa. The university was closed indefinitely after students became violent and torched county lorries. More than 60 students were detained and 50 injured. The students criticised a fees increase of more than Sh7,000, which they say was imposed without consent...Police and the inspectorate department denied the accusations. "There is no arrest that has been reported," Mombasa police boss Martin Asin said..."

"Hundreds of suppliers, contractors and residents demanding their dues yesterday ejected Embu speaker Justus Mate from his office. Mate has blocked the Sh800 million supplementary budget so there is no money to pay the debts. Carrying crude weapons and placards written 'Mate Must Go', the demonstrators forced their way into the assembly despite the presence of armed police officers. They headed straight to Mate's office. He jumped over a wall and escaped...The suppliers tried in vain to break the burglar-prove door to his office in the 10.30am incident. The demonstrators nailed timber bars on the door to keep Mate away. Others broke a window pane and threw undergarments and placards into the office as riot police watched helplessly...The MCAs accused Mate of deliberately blocking the supplementary budget to allocate funds not spent in the last financial year..."

"Meanwhile, more than 500 residents from Mokowe and local administrators on Friday staged a demonstration to protest against drug peddling. They accused police of laxity and colluding with drug barons. The demonstrators demolished kiosks believed to be owned by drug peddlers in Majengo village. "We are doomed if this drug business continues. We have lost and are still losing our children. Our sons are now slowly being turned into zombies, who can't think of nothing else but drugs," resident Asman Omari said. He said if the police can't do their work, "we are glad to be of help". Lamu senior chief Abdalla Shahasi urged addicts to surrender themselves to the county government for rehabilitation..."

"Transport was halted for two hours on Saturday as residents barricaded roads with tyres. More than 500 residents carried placards complaining the 15km Mpeketoni Road, which links the town to Lamu, is "highly potholed". They urged the county government to repair it..."

"Kilifi residents yesterday held protests demanding the revival of the cashew nut industry. They demanded the revocation of a 999-year lease of 350 hectares to an investor who is manufacturing tar instead of processing cashew nuts. The dormant Kenya Cashew Nuts Ltd factory is on the land in Kilifi town. The investor goes by the name Millennium Management Ltd. Residents marched to the factory to issue a 14-day ultimatum to the investor to leave. They asked him to hand over the factory to them or they will forcibly take it. They told the investor to seek compensation from the national government and leave...Led by the Kibaoni Ward Progressive Association founder Hamisi Bwalema, the residents accused the investor of frustrating residents. The residents urged President Uhuru Kenyatta to allocate funds to revive the industry the same way he did for Mumias Sugar Company..."

"Hundreds of Mweiga residents in Nyeri county on Tuesday held demonstrations demanding closure of a mega ballast plant over health hazards. They demanded relocation of the plant. The residents of Kwa-Mburu village in Kieni West say it causes too much noise, dust and degrades the soil. They urged the National Environment Management Authority to close the site..."

"Classes at Voi Girl's High School were on Thursday disrupted after students walked away in protest against dust from construction of the standard gauge railway. The school is to be relocated but leaders are yet to agree on the site. On Wednesday, more than 600 girls took to the streets to demand relocation away from the dusty and noisy construction site. They complained of pollution, saying it caused them frequent asthma attacks and other respiratory problems. "We can't concentrate in class because of the noise and dust from the construction," said one student, who spoke to the Star outside Voi subcounty commissioner's offices. The girls demonstrated around Voi town before proceeding to the district education offices and later to the subcounty commissioner's offices..."

"More than 1,500 IDPs, including forest evictees in Uasin Gishu county, are yet to be resettled. The IDPs held a protest march at Burnt Forest on Wednesday, demanding compensation from the government. Paul Tanui and Jane Kirwa, who spoke on behalf of the group, said the government has been biased in the resettlement process...

"Hundreds of farmers who pulled out of coffee cooperatives protested police harassment on Monday. The farmers, drawn from Tharaka-Nithi, Embu, Kirinyaga and Meru counties, convened at Manyatta Shopping Centre in Embu North subcounty to protest. They say the police make illegal arrests on the orders of cooperative officials and politicians...Protestors marched to the Embu North subcounty headquarters to present a petition to the government demanding an end to illegal arrests...At the subcounty headquarters, they were addressed by assistant deputy county commissioner Evans Otieno who told them their grievances will be addressed. He said a meeting will be arranged with government officials to resolve the problem. Otieno urged farmers to be patient."

"Police fired in the air to disperse university students demonstrating in Kakamega over the death of a schoolmate at the Level 5 hospital last Sunday. Officers also lobbed tear gas canisters at the Masinde Muliro University students during the protest on Thursday over the death of their second-year schoolmate. Abigael Ng'asia, who had delivered a baby at Kakamega Level 5 Hospital, reportedly died days later after a 12-hour wait. Patient Elizabeth Akala died three weeks ago after allegedly waiting 14 hours. The hundreds of students, who waved twigs, stormed the county headquarters at about 9.30am demanding to submit their memorandum to Governor Wycliffe Oparanya. Security officers kept them off as the Governor was driven from the premises, but they marched to the hospital to which regular and AP officers denied them access. Outside the hospital's gate, superintendent Augustine Ajevi told the students investigations into Ng'asia's death were launched, but they responded by hurling stones into the compound. Leader Felix Koech said they were displeased that students who sought treatment at the hospital were allegedly neglected. "We have raised this issue with the Governor more than once but nothing has happened. We are demanding that he sacks all those behind the deaths or we shall physically eject them from office," he said. Police kept guard around Kakamega town to keep the students from regrouping..."

"Hundreds of traders took to the streets on Friday morning protesting the demolition of kiosks in Ruiru, Kiambu county. The traders lit bonfires on the major roads disrupting traffic on the highway and engaged police, who tried to disperse them using tear gas, in running battles. The traders claimed the county government did not give any notice of the Friday morning demolitions..."

"Hundreds of fish traders and employees of a fish processing factory in Kisumu town yesterday held a peaceful demonstration to protest the factory's closure. The traders and the employees marched from the Victoria Delight Fish Factory in Industrial Area to the town centre through Obote and Oginga Odinga streets. They marched to Governor Jack Ranguma's office to seek his audience, but did not find him. They said the factory was closed abruptly on October 31 without employees being informed...Kisumu East subcounty AP boss Karanja Muiru and Kisumu Town chief Willis Anyona helped to calm down the protesters who blocked the entrance to the governor's office."

"Residents of Nayeni, Kilifi county, yesterday held a peaceful demo in Malindi town, protesting against the grabbing of 230 acres. The 200 said 1,800 residents have been rendered squatters. They accused the National Land Commission of failing to take action against the alleged grabbers..."

"Parents held a protest march in Nairobi city centre yesterday to oppose the Sex Education Bill. The bill was proposed by nominated Senator Judith Sijeny. The parents marched from Uhuru Park to Jogoo House chanting "Sijeny must go". They filed a petition with the Education ministry calling for the shelving of the bill..."

"Boda Boda operators lit bonfires on roads in Gatundu South in a protest over MP Moses Kuria's detention on Wednesday. They disrupted business at a taxi bay and marched to the local police station before moving to the Thika/Juja junction but did not damage any property. The youths questioned why Kuria, who is accused of inciting area youths to violence during a past function, was detained yet othersfacing similar charges are free. Kuria was remanded to Kilimani police station on Wednesday after denying incitement charges over the panga remarks he allegedly issued in July..."

"MCAs and residents of Elgeyo Marakwet on Friday held demonstrations to protest against a government plan to declare Kaptagat Forest a water tower. They gave Governor Alex Tolgos two weeks to rescind his plan or they will carry out more protests. The forest lies in two counties including Uasin Gishu, whose Governor Jackson Mandago also wants it declared a key water source. Leading more than 3,000 residents in the protests, Kaptarakwa MCA Thomas Kigen and Chepkorio's Tecla Cherotich said the plan is political..."

"Twenty six protesters were yesterday arrested by riot police on State House Crescent Road. The group led by political activist Boniface Mwangi were among hundreds of protesters who marched on the streets in Nairobi to condemn corruption in government...The group started the peaceful march at Freedom Corner in Uhuru Park and proceeded to Supreme Court where they handed a petition to Chief Justice Willy Mutunga. They then headed to Parliament Buildings. Dressed in red, black and white T-shirts and waving placards reading "knockout corruption" the group left Parliament headed for State House. Their attempts to march on to State House were, however, thwarted by riot police. The group demanded that President Uhuru Kenyatta forms a corruption control council to fight graft in government..."

"Hundreds of Gachie residents from Kiambaa constituency yesterday protested against rise in crime, accusing police of laxityÃ¢ÂÂ¦They said crime increased after the area, which was being manned by Gigiri police station in Nairobi, was referred to Karuri police station in Kiambu county, they said. The Karuri police station is 4km away and officers take too long to respond to distress calls, residents said. They marched to Gigiri police station...OCPD Vitalis Andege calmed the protesters and said he will work with Kiambu police to improve security."

"Kiharu MP Irungu Kang'ata has accused Murang'a Water and Sanitation Company of bribing a resident to drop a suit against a water tariff increase. The MP was leading a protest march in Murang'a town on Friday to condemn the water bills increaseÃ¢ÂÂ¦"

"More than 500 residents of Kwa Mang'eli village in Athi River subcounty want compensation for property destroyed for the standard gauge railway project. They held a march in Athi River town on Monday. The residents demanded compensation for land, crops, trees, vegetables and fruits destroyed during demolitions to pave way for the project...Speaking on behalf of the residents after the two-hour march, he said it has taken too long for the government to fulfil its promise..."We are calling for the national government's intervention so KRC pays us what rightfully belongs to us," he said. The demonstrators blocked the road linking Athi River town to Mombasa Road at Stage 39 bridge, where construction is underway...They gave a police officer manning the site a hard time before he pushed them back..."

Protester Group Identity: widows, disabled, parents & guardians of orphans, vulnerable children
Notes: "BUSINESS yesterday came to a standstill in Keringet town, Nakuru county, as hundreds of demonstrators protested against neglect by the county and national governments. The widows, disabled, parents and guardians of orphans and vulnerable children marched to the deputy county commissioner's office to be addressed. They accused the two governments of not providing money from the Cash Transfer Funds meant for them. The protesters said Kuresoi, Keringet ward, is not benefitting from the national and county governments funds. They urged the government to set aside funds for the poor widows and widowers, regardless of their age, saying most of them are weak, poor and unable to take care of their children...Assistant deputy county commissioner Yasmin Musembi told the protesters the government has factors to consider to make when disbursing the money. She said no cash is set aside for widows."

"Hundreds of Kisumu residents and ODM supporters on Monday took to the streets protesting EACC's move to summon Cord leader Raila Odinga. Wielding twigs, the protesters chanted pro-Raila and ODM slogans as they marched from Kondele to Kisumu Central Business District..."

Police fired tear gas and beat demonstrators with truncheons to stop them storming offices of the electoral commission in Nairobi on Monday. A video shows a man in a green sweatshirt running from police and falling to the ground. Three officers take turns striking him with batons and kicking his motionless body as it lies slumped on the kerb. "TheÂ protestÂ was legitimate, it was a sign of Kenya's hunger for free and fair elections but the response from police was shocking," said Meluleki Mthembu from the African Democratic Institute, based in Johannesburg. "Not even claims of looting by protesters justifies such brutality."

The worst of Monday's confrontations occurred in Nairobi, the capital, when protesters tried to march on the offices of the independent electoral and boundaries commission. Police had banned the plannedÂ demonstrationÂ and scores of officers inÂ riotÂ gear guarded the building. A water cannon truck later forced the convoy of vehicles carrying opposition leaders and supporters accompanying it on foot out of the city centre, witnesses said. Earlier, police said they had arrested seven people in Mombasa where otherÂ protestsÂ took place.

The protesters demanded that commission members quit before elections next year and set tyres alight, blocking roads. Monday deadlyÂ protestsÂ rocked several areas of Kenya, government security officials issued a decree on Tuesday banning all ''unlawfulÂ demonstrations.'' In Kisumu, in western Kenya, the police battled mobs, shooting several people. The government said on Tuesday that 50 people had been injured and two killed, and it blamed the protesters for the violence. Witnesses in Kisumu said police officers had opened fire on a crowd, hitting a 5-year-old boy in the back.

Four officers have been arrested and the case has exploded like few others inÂ Kenya, provoking marches,Â protests,Â the involvement of the F.B.I. and outrage that has turned into violence. Hordes of young men stormed a police station this week andÂ burnedÂ the metal container where the victims had been secretly held. Lawyers vowed to boycott the courts for a week, out of solidarity for their fallen colleague, and their absence has paralyzed Kenya's justice system.
About 300 people marched through Nairobi on July 4 toÂ protestÂ the men's disappearances, and demanded that the interior minister, Joseph Nkaissery, resign.

Location of Protest: Mathari National Teaching and Referral Hospital
Notes: A national strike among medical workers led to at least 87 patients fleeing Kenya's only psychiatric hospital after being left unattended. Seventeen were brought back to Mathari National Teaching and Referral Hospital yesterday. Police fired tear gas to disperse doctors protesting about salaries. Union leaders say new doctors with six years' training get less than police recruits.

The doctors, who have brought city centres to a standstill with regularÂ protestÂ marches, say the dispute is not about salaries alone: they are also demanding that hospitals be better equipped, and patients given better treatment.

"Thousands of medical workers at the 5,000-bed Muhimbili Medical Center (MMC) demonstrated in front of the prime minister's office after an emergency meeting decided friday morning to back the dismissed medical personnel."

"tanzanian police fired tear gas in downtown dar es salaam on saturday to disperse demonstrators who demand the release of christopher mtikila, leader of the provisionally-registered democratic party (dp). at least one person was arrested when policemen in riot gear blocked the procession at the junction of morogoro road and uwt street in the city center and fired tear gas at the marchers, the local "sunday news" reported today."

"five teachers who were held by police in connection with an alleged illegal demonstration in dar es salaam on thursday were released on police bonds. about 400 teachers from primary and secondary schools and colleges in the city took part in the demonstration."

"The students' strike began here on Oct. 6 when they invaded the headquarters of the Ministry of Science, Technology and Higher Education, pressing for payment of their allowances. Tanzanian government authorities had to deploy riot police to disperse the students who had surrounded the ministry buildings."

"Dar-es-Salaam - Riots in the densely populated Kinondoni district of Dar-es-Salaam on February 13 in which two people died, dozens were injured and 130 arrested, were said to involve "Muslim zealots," the jobless, homeless, school drop-outs and drug addicts."

"Dar es Salaam (AANA) - Thousands of Muslim fundamentalists in the Tanzanian capital, Dar es Salaam, brought parts of the city around Mwembe Chai Mosque to a stand still on May 29 after they rioted and set government vehicles on fire. The Muslims were angered by the recall of a permit granted to Muslim women to meet at a public hall in town. The women's agenda included what they said was mistreatment by police last February after the police arrested women demonstrators during a street protest."

Fifteen civilians and 14 policemen were injured in a riot in Zanzibar on Wednesday when 18 opposition Civil United Front (CUF) members were brought to court to answer treason charges, local media reported on Thursday. Zanzibar Assistant Commissioner of Police Juma Mtumwa was quoted as saying that 40 people had been arrested and would soon appear in court.

POLICE clashed with demonstrators in Zanzibar yesterday as anger boiled over at government fraud in Sunday's presidential elections. Police in full riot gear fired live rounds in the air and used tear gas to disperse a crowd of about 300 mainly young people who had started to throw stones at a police car on the outskirts of Stone Town. A small group of demonstrators took refuge in nearby buildings but were forced out by police who beat them with batons. Several were arrested and driven away by police.

Protesters seeking new elections fought running battles with the police today as violence spread across Tanzania and left as many as 17 people dead.  Opposition officials and doctors said 16 protesters had been killed on Zanzibar's main islands of Unguja and Pemba as demonstrations across the archipelago calling for a rerun of disputed elections turned violent. One member of the security forces was decapitated, a police official said.

More than 50,000 protesters marched through the Tanzanian capital, Dar es Salaan, as one of Africa's most united countries moved further towards possible disintegration, writes Jane Astill.  The marchers wanted a rerun of elections last year in the semi-autonomous Zanzibar islands. Opposition groups say the voting was rigged by the ruling Chama Cha Mapinduzi Party.

At least 50,000 people marched yesterday in the first joint opposition demonstration on Zanzibar since the controversial October elections that international observers described as fundamentally flawed. Demonstrators from six opposition parties marched to Maisara grounds, where they held a rally demanding new elections for the semiautonomous archipelago in Tanzania.

Tanzanian police on Saturday dispersed dozens of opposition supporters who had attempted to protest the government's decision to buy a controversial air traffic control system from Britain, witnesses said. They said about 100 supporters of the opposition Tanzania Labour Party (TLP) had gathered at TLP offices in Dar es Salaam around midday, but were dispersed by anti-riot police.

Hundreds of workers of Tanzania's Electric Supply Company (TANESCO) staged a demonstration at the firm's head office here Thursday to protest its takeover by a South African firm, officials and witnesses said. The government appointed Net Group Solution on April 2 to run TANESCO before it is privatised, but workers at the state firm are demanding payment of their benefits before the new management takes over Thursday.

Hundreds of workers of Tanzania's state-owned power utility, Electric Supply Company (TANESCO), Wednesday marked May Day by staging a demonstration against South African managers. Instead of going to the Dar es Salaam National Stadium to march with other workers in the official a May Day parade, the singing, dancing and placard-waving demonstrators, gathered at TANESCO head office to protest against the takeover of TANESCO by South African managers.

Tanzania's anti-riot police have dispersed a demonstration staged by students of the University of Dar Es Salaam and made some 50 arrests, local newspaper Daily News reported Wednesday. The students gathered Tuesday on the campus in a protest of the Higher Education Students' Loan Bill which was passed by the National Assembly on Monday.

Police opened fire on protesters at a voter registration center in an opposition stronghold of Zanzibar on Wednesday, killing three people and wounding dozens of others, police said. Regional police commander Faraji Kayuga said officers opened fire when confronted by protesters at a center in Ngombeni on the northern Zanzibari island of Pemba. Opposition members tried to prevent the armed riot police from entering the center, Kayuga said.

Soldiers have fired shots and teargas to disperse opposition protesters at a Zanzibar polling station as sporadic violence and charges of fraud marred elections on the volatile Tanzanian archipelago. The violence erupted as the main opposition party on Zanzibar denounced what it said was widespread fraud in Sunday's election and alleged the ruling party was trying to "cook the results".

More than 500 residents from areas affected by the Mbagala [arms depot] explosions in Dar es Salaam have come out to protest saying the probe team investigating the impact of the explosion to property and buildings did not seek their views.

Riot police in Zanzibar fired tear gas to disperse residents of Tumbatu Island in North Unguja who stormed a voter registration centre yesterday demanding to be registered without the Zanzibar Residence IDs.

The construction of the 65km-Tanga - Horohoro Highway took a new turn at the weekend after a group of villagers closed a section of it demanding that the new road should pass through their village. Vehicles, including buses plying between Tanga and Mombasa in Kenya, were held for almost five hours at Mabokweni village as villagers camped at the middle of the road pressing their demand.

The Prevention and Combating of Corruption Bureau (PCCB) has warned pressure groups against attempts to use it for their own interests. The anti corruption watchdog was reacting to Chadema supporters' allegations that it has been lenient in acting on corruption tip-offs in political campaigns. Said the Arusha regional PCCB commander, Mr Ayoub Akida, recently: "We don't want to be used by a faction of people who may have malicious interests.

Location of Protest: Mwanza, Dar Es Salaam, Kahama, Arusha, Busanda, Tarime and in Zanzibar
Notes: Chaos reigned in Mwanza City and other lake zone districts yesterday as impatient youths protested the delay in announcing election results by the National Electoral Commission (NEC) officials. Two vehicles, a Nissan Patrol and a saloon car said to belong to Ilemela deputy returning officer Paulo Masangu, were torched using a petrol bomb while as many as 10 other cars had their windows smashed with stones as thousands of Opposition supporters in Ilemela and Nyamagana constituencies demanded the immediate release of poll results.

Thousands of Arusha residents thronged the city hall throughout Monday demanding prompt release of the results causing the police to deploy teams of anti-riot squads equipped with all necessary weapons including, tear gas canisters and the menacing, armored Dong-feng Winnebago truck that sprays stingy liquid.

Police fired in the air to disperse hundreds of opposition supporters who were yesterday planning to demonstrate in Dar es Salaam in support of calls for a new constitution. A dozen members of the Civic United Front (CUF) were arrested when they engaged the police in a cat-and-mouse chase along the busy city streets for most of the morning hours as they attempted to march to the Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs.

The Leader of the Official Opposition in Parliament, Mr Freeman Mbowe, was among four Chadema MPs detained by police after a demonstration called by the opposition party was violently broken up yesterday. Other MPs who were being held at Central Police Station in Arusha were Mr Godbless Lema (Arusha), Mr Joseph Selasini (Rombo) and Mr Philemon Ndesamburo (Moshi Urban). A section of the busy Arusha-Moshi highway turned into a battlefield as heavily armed riot police moved in to break up the demonstration led by senior Chadema officials. Several of the party's leaders were arrested, and dozens of people, including journalists, beaten up and injured by baton-wielding police officers. Police also fired in the air, sending people scurrying for cover.

The Police Force yesterday used tear gas, water cannons and pepper spray to disperse hundreds of University of Dar es Salaam (UDSM) students who were matching to the State House to present their demands for increased meals allowance. The students engaged the law enforcers in a running battle at Survey area, where the Field Force Unit (FFU) confronted the students. The students have boycotted classes since Thursday to press for increases of meals allowance from the current Sh5,000 to Sh10,000 per day, citing increase in cost of living.

Activities in most of Mwanza came to a standstill yesterday afternoon as people took part in a peaceful demonstration organised by Chadema.The demonstration was led by Mr Mbowe, who is also leader of official opposition in the Parliament. He was flanked by Dr Slaa and almost all Chadema MPs. There were only few uniformed policemen and Chadema's Red Brigade took charge of security during the demonstrations and at the rally. The demonstration started at around 1pm at Buzuruga primary school and went through Musoma, Pamba, Kenyata and Makongoro roads before it climaxed at Furahisha grounds at around 3.45pm.Addressing the rally earlier, the Kawe MP, Ms Halima Mdee, urged Tanzanians to shun fear and confront the government when it does not deliver. "It took a young man who set himself on fire to overthrow corrupt governments in Tunisia and Egypt. Time to fear is long gone," she said.

Several people were reportedly injured when the police used live ammunition and tear gas canisters to disperse petty traders who were protesting the demolition of the Manzese second-hand clothes market. The fracas erupted after the traders blocked a section of Morogoro road in protest of the demolition. After arriving at around 11am yesterday to find about 100 stalls on the ground, the traders protested the move by blocking the road with logs and other debris. The police moved in and fired several warning shots in the air and tear gas canisters to the traders to disperse them

Thousands of Mbeya residents yesterday thronged city streets in peaceful demonstrations organised by the opposition Chama cha Demokrasia na Maendeleo (Chadema) to protest the increasing cost of living.The demonstrations, which started at Mafiati and climaxed at CCM grounds, were led by Chadema national chairman Freeman Mbowe who is also the leader of official Opposition in Parliament. Other leaders who participated in the demonstrations were Chadema secretary general Willibrod Slaa, outspoken Arusha Urban MP Godbless Lema and his Mbeya Urban counterpart Joseph Mbilinyi.

Police here were forced to use teargas to disperse rioters during the early morning hours of yesterday following a strike by commuter bus operators over alleged harassment by the law keepers. Until late in the afternoon, however, there were no reports of injuries, but several government vehicles had their windscreens smashed by mobs of rioters. Also smashed were the glass windows of a motor vehicle showroom along the Dodoma Road.

Police in Arumeru District, Arusha Region were at the weekend forced to fire tear gas and live bullets into the air to disperse angry people fighting over water at Kikwe and Nambala villages. The confrontation came about when the law enforcers blocked the villagers from using the water from the nearby rivers, which is increasingly dwindling due to drought, to irrigate their farms.

About 46 University of Dar es Salaam students were arrested yesterday after staging a demonstration to pile pressure on the government to disburse loans to all deserving students.The early morning protest was in solidarity with nearly 4,000 of their colleagues countrywide who have reportedly been denied state funding for their higher education requirements this financial year.

Protester Group Identity: Legal and Human Rights Centre (LHRC), Tanzania Gender Networking Programme (TGNP) and Tanzania Media Women Association (Tamwa)
Notes: The ongoing doctors' strike took a dramatic twist yesterday when activists in Dar es Salaam took to the streets to protest what they termed government's failure to address the crisis decisively and avert deaths and suffering. This comes in the aftermath of a Cabinet meeting that took place in Dodoma on Tuesday evening chaired by Prime Minister, Mr Mizengo Pinda, who then flew to Dar es Salaam the next morning. His office did not, however, give details on the purpose of the impromptu journey. In Dar es Salaam the activists blocked a section of Ali Hassan Mwinyi Road at the busy Selander Bridge intersection for about an hour before police persuaded them to disperse. The marchers carried placards that criticised the government, accusing it of indecisiveness in the face of the ongoing doctors' strike as innocent Tanzanians continued to die at Muhimbili National Hospital. However, before they dispersed, the activists from 14 civil society organisations gave the government 24 hours to resolve the crisis. Should the government fail to do to so, they vowed, marchers would return to the streets. Their placards carried several messages including those calling on President Jakaya Kikwete to fire top official in the ministry of Health and Social Welfare, including Minister Hadji Mponda, his deputy Dr Lucy Nkya, Permanent Secretary Blandina Nyoni and the Chief Government Medical Officer Dr Deo Mutasiwa.

Police in Songea allegedly shot dead four civilians yesterday, during a fracas associated with a public demonstration against a reported string of murders over the past four months, that the law enforcement organ is accused of neither curbing nor resolving.In a quick rejoinder, however, Ruvuma Regional Police Commander Michael Kamuhanda put the figure of those who had died at two. Several other people were injured when police officers used tear gas and live ammunition to quell angry demonstrators, some of whom had stormed the town's main police station.The Ruvuma regional hospital chief medical officer, Dr Benedicto Ngaiza, confirmed that the hospital had received four bodies and about 20 injured persons.

Muslim protesters clashed with police in the commercial capital, Dar es Salaam, today during a protest over the arrest of an Islamic cleric. Police fired tear gas and at least 30 people were arrested.  Similar demonstrations have erupted sporadically in recent weeks, raising religious tensions in the relatively stable and secular East African country.  Sheikh Ponda Issa Ponda was arrested last month and charged with theft and trespass.

"A thousand Burundi university students held a silent protest Friday after the election that gave the central African country its first president from the Hutu majority, Melchior Ndadaye. Students from different ethnic groups took part in the demonstration, where the watchword was that "only the banners should speak," according to witnesses. Banners dismissed the vote as an "ethnic census of Burundi."

"Up to 5,000 people, some ripping up their voter's card, demonstrated here Saturday to protest the "ethnic-based" election of Melchior Ndadaye as Burundi's first president from the Hutu ethnic majority. The protestors from the minority Tutsi ethnic group carried banners attacking the "ethnic character" of the election, which gave Ndadaye a 64.79 percent victory in Tuesday's poll, according the latest official results published Saturday."
"Some 2,000 Tutsi college and school students demonstrated in the capital earlier Tuesday against Ndadaye's election. On Monday, police broke up a similar demonstration with tear gas."
"A number of protestors were killed in the Burundi capital Bujumbura during a demonstration against the overthrow of President Melchior Ndadaye, Bishop Alfred Ndoricimpa said here Friday."

"Nearly 1,000 youths marched through Burundi's capital Sunday in a demonstration against the coup in which president Melchior Ndadaye was reported killed, as four political parties called for a general strike."

"Around 10,000 people staged a silent demonstration here Tuesday against the military coup that has sparked a new wave of ethnic violence in Burundi. Demonstrators walked through the streets of the Burundian capital that were otherwise quiet with public transport at a halt."

"More than 10,000 Burundis calmly took to the streets here Thursday to urge government ministers to come out of hiding after last week's coup attempt, as the army chief assured the elected authorities of his support."

"Thousands of anti-government demonstrators took to the streets here to protest plans to deploy Organisation of African Unity (OAU) troops in Burundi in a bid to restore confidence in the wake of widespread ethnic carnage. Answering an appeal by seven anti-government parties, the demonstrators protested Sunday the planned arrival of a 200-stong OAU protection force, including 180 soldiers, shouting slogans claiming the deployment would turn Burundi into a second Somalia."

"Thousands of opposition supporters erected barricades in Burundi's capital Bujumbura on Thursday to protest the planned arrival of United Nations forces, relief officials said. Shops, schools and offices were closed, and young protesters manning barricades on the three main roads into Bujumbura prevented traffic from leaving or entering the capital, said the officials, contacted by telephone in Bujumbura."

Protester Group Identity: opponents of assassinated Burundi president Melchior Ndaday
Notes: "Around 2,000 opponents of assassinated Burundi president Melchior Ndadaye held a demonstration here Wednesday demanding what they called the immediate restoration of "constitutional legality.""

"The detention order against Mathias Hitimana, who heads the People's Reconciliation Party (PRP), was served Sunday hours after around 500 youths held a demonstration in central Bujumbura to protest the arrest of seven students, the source said." "Police dispersed Sunday's demonstration with tear gas after the protestors erected street barricades in outlying districts of the city."

"Burundian students pursued a protest strike against the government on Friday, raising the tension in a country fearful of an ethnic bloodbath after a murderous grenade attack in the capital. The students, mainly Tutsi supporters of opposition parties, demanded the release of politician Mathias Hitimana, arrested on Sunday after he organised a student demonstration which left 17 people dead."

Protester Group Identity: Supporters of Tutsi-dominated main opposition party
Notes: "Supporters of Burundi's Tutsi-dominated main opposition party rallied Monday for a protest march to demand the resignation of the country's parliamentary speaker whom they accuse of inciting ethnic bloodshed."

"Burundian President Sylvestre Ntibantunganya renewed support for his prime minister on Saturday as several hundred opposition members converged on central Bujumbura to demand the premier's dismissal."

"With the tiny central African nation on the brink of a bloodbath, the 2,000 to 3,000 students accused the envoy, Ahmedou Ould Abdallah of Mauritania, of siding with armed Hutu extremists. The students also demanded the resignation of President Sylvestre Ntibantunganya, a Hutu, unless he provided details of the provenance of the arms being used by Hutu gangs in clashes with Tutsi militias which are sharpening fears that Burundi may plunge into full-scale civil war comparable to the one which tore neighbouring Rwanda apart last year."

Protester Group Identity: Tutsi university and secondary school students
Notes: "Some 3,000 university and secondary school students marched through Burundi's capital Tuesday, demanding justice for killers involved in mass slayings two years ago."
