That forced the group to march on along Jalan Sultan Ismail towards the focal point in Padang Merbok, but it seemed that some had other ideas as a group began to converge at the entrance of Chinatown in Petaling Street, which was also guarded by a strong police presence, later reinforced by several FRU units, as the crowd began to turn unruly..."; 3) "recited 14 resolutions for the Red Shirts rally-goers to follow...He said the resolutions also included calls to reject racism; foreign intervention in national affairs; action against illegal rallies; accepting Islam as the official religion of the country; supporting the government during economic difficulties; defending Malay and Bumiputera rights; defending the elected government; and restoring the Internal Security Act..."

"The "Save Selangor from the Pakatan government rally" kicked off yesterday, but not at its planned venue. The rally, held at the Ampang Umno division building instead of the Spectrum shopping mall in Ampang Jaya here, saw about 200 protesters voicing out their dissatisfaction with the state government. The speakers highlighted the state government's dismal record in helping people in Selangor own affordable houses, as well as issues related to solid waste management, potholes, existence of numerous illegal gambling and vice dens, dengue epidemic and the recent toll hike...Protesters, mostly wearing red shirts with the words "Selamatkan Negeri Selangor dari Pakatan Cacar Marbar" (Save Selangor from the chaotic opposition), started chanting "Hidup Rakyat" (long live the people) at 3pm in front of the parking area of the building..."

"MORE than 200 cabbies converged at Padang Merbok here to protest against the Land Public Transport Commission (SPAD) yesterday. The rally, organised by the Taxi Drivers Action Committee (JBPTLK), was to demand the resignation of SPAD chairman Tan Sri Syed Hamid Albar, a revamp of SPAD and the banning of ride-sharing services GrabCar and Uber..."

"Some 200 people staged a two-hour peaceful protest at the main entrance of the state legislative assembly building here over the meeting between PKR vice-president Nurul Izzah Anwar and self-styled Sulu princess Jacel Kiram yesterday. The group comprising members of the public and non-governmental organisation representatives, led by Pakatan Pro-Barisan Nasional president Zulkarnain Mahdar who spoke at the gathering, handed a letter of protest to a representative of assembly speaker Datuk Syed Abas Syed Ali. They called for the state assembly, currently in session, to approve a motion banning the Lembah Pantai member of parliament and PKR vice-president Tian Chua, who was reported to have arranged the meeting between Nurul Izzah and Jacel, from entering Sabah..."

Location of Protest: Kota Darul Naim state secretariat building complex, Kota Baru
Notes: More than 100 people gathered peacefully at the state secretariat building complex, Kota Darul Naim here, yesterday, to protest the ban on the sale of vape and other items, effective from this month.  The protesters gathered in a park in front of the building at 2pm.   Policemen were on hand to handle the crowd but there were no untoward incidents.  The crowd dispersed at 3.15pm after Mohd Khaleb Khan Nasir Khan, the spokesman for Solidarity V Kelantan, a group comprising vape sellers and users, handed a memorandum and  a petition, signed by 1,000 users and traders, to the Kelantan Menteri Besar's press secretary, Asri Awang.

Protester Group Identity: Non-governmental organisations Kongres Rakyat and Bantah TPPA
Notes: A rally to protest against the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) agreement was held at Padang Merbok yesterday.  Co-organised by non-governmental organisations (NGOs), Kongres Rakyat and Bantah TPPA, and supported by other NGOs, the protesters gathered at five venues, before converging at the field at 2pm.  However, about 300 people were reported to have gathered at Dataran Merdeka even though City Hall had allowed the event to take place only at Padang Merbok.

Protester Group Identity: A group led by former Penang Island City Council (MBPP) councillor Iszuree Ibrahim
Notes: Former Penang Island City Council (MBPP) councillor Iszuree Ibrahim led a group of 50 people yesterday to protest against the state government's plan to carry out a reclamation project along the Permatang Damar Laut coast.  Iszuree, who is also Penang Pas secretary, said the project, slated under the RM27 billion Penang Transport Master Plan (PTMP), should be scrapped to preserve marine life and the fishing communities' source of income.  The proposed land reclamation would see the construction of three man-made islands some 300m from the shores of Teluk Kumbar, Gertak Sanggul and Bayan Lepas under PTMP.

Protester Group Identity: Barisan Nasional Youth leaders and representatives from non-governmental organisations
Notes: Some 500 people gathered outside the Taman Manggis land fronting Jalan Burma here yesterday to demand Chief Minister Lim Guan Eng step down over the low-cost housing fiasco in the state.  The Taman Manggis land, where flats for poor people were supposed to be built, was sold to a company whose shareholder was purportedly linked to the previous owner of Lim's bungalow in Jalan Pinhorn, which he bought for RM2.8 million last year.    Emotions ran high during the 30-minute protest as state Barisan Nasional Youth leaders and representatives from non-governmental organisations spoke out against Lim, who is also DAP secretary-general.  Those present held placards denouncing Lim for failing to address housing woes in the state.  The group dispersed at 3pm.

Location of Protest: Bukit Bintang, KLCC and KL Sentral in Kuala Lumpur
Notes: A PROTEST by hundreds of taxi drivers in Bukit Bintang, KLCC and KL Sentral here yesterday ended with five of them being arrested and two taxis seized by police.  The rally was to protest against Uber and GrabCar ride-sharing services. It started in Jalan Ampang at 10am before protesters headed for Jalan Bukit Bintang and parked their taxis in front of a supermarket.  More than 100 taxis parked on the road, causing a massive traffic jam. Police had to divert traffic leading to Jalan Bukit Bintang.  The taxis seized were parked in the middle of the road, forcing authorities to tow them away to end the standstill.  Jalan Bukit Bintang was reopened to traffic at 12.30pm.  It is learnt that those arrested included Persatuan Transformasi Pemandu Teksi Malaysia (Pers1m) president Kamaruddin Mohd Hussain.  "I feel that it was my obligation to join in the protest to ensure the survival of taxi drivers.  "I don't care who organised the event. They want a total ban on Uber and GrabCar services and I support that."

Almost 200 fishermen from three villages in Sungai Masai have seen their catch dwindle for the past seven years due to pollution.  The local council said the black and foul smelling water in some parts of the river was likely due to food waste from a nearby wet market and grime from lorry-washing centres.  Southern Johor Fishermen Association chairman Azli Mohd Aziz said its members had experienced a 30 per cent decrease in their catch.  "The problem began in 2009 when the river water turned blackish. The situation forced many fishermen to venture further, nearer to Singapore or Pengerang, Kota Tinggi, as there is hardly any catch here," said Azli after a peaceful demonstration by fishermen at the Kampung Pasir Gudang Baru jetty on Thursday.  He said residents were told that the pollution was allegedly caused by sewage from a septic tank in Taman Bukit Dahlia, and that they were frustrated that their complaints had fallen on deaf ears.  Pasir Gudang Municipal Council president Md Za'nal Misran said the local council would use microorganism technology to clean the river.  Malaysian Nature Society Johor chairman Vincent Chow said the authorities should carry out strict enforcement to prevent the illegal dumping of waste into the river.

Protester Group Identity: Anti - Goods and Services Tax (GST) protesters
Notes: The anti-GST rally on Saturday has been proven unsuccessful judging from the low turnout of only 1,800 participants, said Pas deputy president Datuk Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man.  He said the campaign could only be described as otherwise in terms of traction, if people were to consider that it was Pas which spearheaded protests against the implementation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST).  "We were not invited to participate in the rally. However, we have been campaigning against GST since the very beginning, including holding demonstrations. We have already sent a message to the government.  "Pas members, too, are aware of the matter and the party's stand. They opted to stay out of the rally without the party having to issue any instruction," said Tuan Ibrahim.  Tuan Ibrahim said Pas was preoccupied with its branch meetings, preparations for the Sarawak polls and organising protest against the implementation of Dual Language Programme (DLP) in schools on Saturday.

Protester Group Identity: Former estate workers in Hulu Selangor and Kuala Selangor
Notes: Left with just two days, 57 former estate workers in Hulu Selangor and Kuala Selangor are demanding the Selangor government's intervention to ensure they are not forced out of their homes.  The former estate workers of Ladang Mary, Ladang Sungai Tinggi, Ladang Bukit Tagar, Ladang Nigel Gardner and Ladang Minyak received eviction notices last month, ordering them to move out of their quarters by tomorrow.  The news was met with dissatisfaction as the promise of low-cost homes has not been fulfilled.  Yesterday, the former workers held a peaceful protest at the entrance of the State Secretariat building here.  They came with a memorandum addressed to Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Azmin Ali and Plantation Workers, Poverty and Caring Government Committee chairman Ganabatirau Veraman.  Parti Sosialis Malaysia supreme council member S. Arulchelvan, whom the former estate workers had turned to for assistance, handed over the memorandum to Ganabatirau's policy adviser, K. Vasantha Kumar.  Arulchelvan said the eviction should be postponed or cancelled until a housing solution was found.

Location of Protest: From Jalan Setiabakti to the site of a proposed high-rise condominium in Jalan Setiakasih, Kuala Lumpur
Notes: SOME 250 residents of Bukit Damansara marched in protest against a 23-storey luxury condominium project yesterday.  Organised by the Bukit Damansara House Owners' Association, the one kilometre walk took participants from Jalan Setiabakti to the site of the proposed high-rise condominium in Jalan Setiakasih.  Association chairman Tan Sri Abdul Aziz Abdul Rahman said residents were protesting against the haphazard development that was incompatible with their neighbourhood, which was a low-rise, low density area.  "This is supported by the Kuala Lumpur 2020 City Plan draft, which clearly limits the neighbourhood's density to 24 people per 0.4ha," said Aziz.  "The residents are calling on City Hall to gazette the plan and reject the proposal to build luxury condominiums in Bukit Damansara. Do not spoil this peaceful low-rise, low-density area."

Location of Protest: Taman Tun Dr Ismail (TTDI), Kuala Lumpur
Protester Group Identity: Residents of Taman Tun Dr Ismail (TTDI)
Notes: Residents of Taman Tun Dr Ismail (TTDI) gathered at Taman Rimba Kiara yesterday to stage a peaceful protest against a new development project in the park.  TTDI residents association chairman Abdul Hafiz Abu Bakar announced two objectives during the protest - to call for Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) to stop receiving plans for development in the park and to gazette the public park as a public open space.  "The move to gazette the park as a public open space has been long overdue. There will be threats of development (in this park) until it is gazetted," he said, adding that they had also urged the authorities to proceed with the redevelopment of housing for 100 "longhouse" families, promised 30 years ago.  "We are appealing to the authorities to leave Taman Rimba Kiara as a public park for the residents of TTDI. This is where we hold outdoor activities and wedding receptions. We will tabulate the number of signatures on the petition and send it to the authorities tomorrow."  Nearly 500 supporters, ranging from the elderly to children, turned up to protest against the proposed redevelopment of the site to house eight blocks of 54-storey serviced apartments, and a block of apartments with 350 affordable units.  Apart from damage to the park, the redevelopment will raise the density of 60 persons per acre to as high as 979 persons per acre.

Location of Protest: District and land office, Kuala Selangor
Notes: Some 100 residents of Kampung Sungai Yu held a peaceful demonstration in front of the district and land office here yesterday, demanding that the state government review its list of recipients for residential lots meant for underprivileged members of the Indian community.  The demonstrators alleged that the PKR-led state government had conducted the distribution of lots in an unfair and non-transparent manner by awarding them to undeserving parties.  Kampung Sungai Yu residents' representative M. Palanivel said they were shocked to learn that most of the recipients were not local people, including some who are not from Selangor, but from other states such as Negri Sembilan, Penang and Johor.  Palanivel and several other representatives also handed over a three-page memorandum to principal assistant district officer (land division) Mohd Faizal Abdul Raji.

Going to Mid Valley Megamall here is a hassle for wheelchair-bound shoppers, who are forced to cross a busy road outside the shopping mall with the help of auxiliary policemen.  Damai Disabled Person Association Malaysia president V. Murugeswaran, 45, said those on wheelchair arriving from Mid Valley KTM Komuter station would have to seek assistance from the mall authorities to enter the premises safely.  Two auxiliary policemen were stationed at the sidewalk near the Komuter station and the mall's entrance to assist the disabled.  "The Komuter station is just beside the mall but there is no direct entrance for wheelchair-bound visitors. The obstacles, such as the busy road and big dividers, make it difficult to enter the mall.  "The simplest and most immediate solution would be to build a lift at the pedestrian bridge that links the station and the mall's first-floor entrance at the north court."  He was involved in a peaceful demonstration by members of two non-governmental organisations outside the mall's north court entrance here yesterday.  Some 50 members and volunteers of Damai and Dual Blessing Bhd gathered at the venue to demand long-term solutions for this problem as well as the poor accessibility for disabled people in public places in the city.  "We want to live independently but the lack of proper access to these establishments makes it hard for us.  "We hope the authorities will provide permanent solutions to this problem," he said.

Location of Protest: Gurney Drive, George Town; from Menara Umno to Komtar, George Town
Protester Group Identity: People from non-governmental organisations and Umno Youth
Notes: SOME 3,000 people from non-governmental organisations and Umno Youth flooded Gurney Drive on October 1st, demanding that Chief Minister Lim Guan Eng relinquish his post following graft charges against him.  They continuously chanted "Undur Lim Guan Eng" (Step down Lim Guan Eng), "Undur perasuah" (Step down, corrupt), "Hancur DAP" (Destroy DAP) and "Hancur Lim Guan Eng" (Destroy Lim Guan Eng).  They also held banners that read "Guan Eng undur" (Guan Eng step down) and "Polis jangan lulus permit Bersih 5.0" (Police, don't approve Bersih 5.0 permit).  The crowd voiced their dissatisfaction with Lim, who, they said, had put Penang in the spotlight by being its first chief minister to face graft charges.  They also called for him to be booted out in the next general election.  They urged police not to grant a permit to Bersih 5.0 organisers to hold the gathering in the state.  Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mior Faridalatrash Wahid said police would investigate under Section 9(5) of the Peaceful Assembly Act as the organisers had not given any notice on yesterday's gathering.  He said police had identified those who took to the stand to speak and would call them in for questioning.  "However, they abided by our warning when we asked them to disperse," he said, adding that no untoward incident was reported.  ABOUT 3,000 people marched from Menara Umno to Komtar October 26th, calling for Chief Minister Lim Guan Eng's resignation.  Clad in black T-shirts bearing the word "bangkit (rise)", the protesters chanted "Undur (step down) Guan Eng" repeatedly as they raised banners.  The march started about 1.50pm and the group arrived at Komtar 10 minutes later.  The group was led by Umno Youth vice-chief Khairul Azwan Harun and Penang Umno Youth chief Rafizal Abdul Rahim.  "We will hold similar demonstrations if Lim refuses to meet our demand to stay away from the Bersih 5.0 rally," Khairul said.  The crowd dispersed about 2.35pm.

Location of Protest: From the Shah Alam City Council headquarters to the state secretariat, Kuala Lumpur
Notes: The Umno Education Bureau has defended the group involved in a "flying buckets" protest on Tuesday, as people have a right to be angry over water problems in Selangor.  Its chairman, Tan Sri Dr Ibrahim Shah Abu Shah, said he hoped the protest would make Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Azmin Ali aware of the people's anger and find a solution to the issue.  "I think we should support them (the protesters). I'm not angry with the people who expressed their anger towards the menteri besar.  "The water problem is serious. You can't survive without water, it is a basic need in life," he said here yesterday.  Ibrahim said Azmin's claim that Barisan Nasional and Umno had sabotaged his government by contaminating Sungai Semenyih should be investigated and that action should be taken against him if his claim was proven to be false.  About 100 people, led by Umno Youth executive committee member Datuk Armand Azha Abu Hanifah, started marching from the Shah Alam City Council headquarters to the state secretariat.  They demanded the state government resolve the water issues fast instead of blaming the problem on alleged sabotage.  After about 45 minutes, Azmin's political secretary Shuhaimie Shafiei met the protesters before allowing Armand and several others into the compound.  The protesters dispersed around noon.

Tens of thousands of people took to the streets of Kuala Lumpur, the capital of Malaysia, on Saturday to call for the resignation of Prime Minister Najib Razak, who is accused of taking $1 billion from a government investment fund.  The protesters, wearing the yellow T-shirts of Malaysia's clean government movement, known as Bersih, converged on the city center to hear their leaders call for Mr. Najib's ouster. Among the speakers was former Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, 91, who once chose Mr. Najib as prime minister but now criticizes his former protÃ©gÃ©'s government as corrupt.  The authorities had tried to thwart the daylong, peaceful demonstration by arresting at least eight protest leaders on Friday, including Bersih's chairwoman, Maria Chin Abdullah. She was being held under the country's strict Security Offenses Act.  This was the fifth year that Bersih, whose name means ''clean'' in Malay, had staged a protest calling for an end to corruption in government. Bersih also organized smaller protests calling for Mr. Najib's resignation in cities around the world.  POLICE arrested 21 key people connected to the Bersih and Red Shirts movements.  Some had brought children, an offence under the Peaceful Assembly Act 2012 (PAA).  City police chief Datuk Amar Singh said the men who were arrested during the rallies included activist Hishamuddin Rais, Pasir Pinji assemblyman Howard Lee and Red Shirts' prominent figure Datuk Armand Azha Abu Hanifah. Activist Fahmi Reza was nabbed after the Bersih 5 rally ended.  He said of the three others, the first to be arrested was a 49-year-old, who was found to have been using a drone.  Amar said this was an offence under Section 143 of the Civil Aviation Act 1969, which stipulates that the use of an unmanned aircraft or drone in areas where people are gathered requires the approval of the authorities.  Another 33-year-old man was detained under Section 323 of the Penal Code for causing hurt.  Amar said the number of people who attended the Bersih 5 rally was estimated to be 15,500, while about 2,500 Red Shirts supporters took part in the group's counter-rally.

Location of Protest: From Padang Merbok to Parliament House, Kuala Lumpur
Notes: About 300 protesters gathered outside Parliament yesterday to demand the release of Bersih 2.0 chairman Maria Chin Abdullah, who was detained under the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act (Sosma) 2012 on Friday, a day before the coalition's rally in the city.  The group, mostly made up of women, made its way from Padang Merbok to Parliament House at 10.45am.  The protest was led by former Bersih chairman Datuk S. Ambiga, G25 spokesman Datuk Noor Farida Ariffin and former Women's Aid Organisation head Ivy Josiah.  Among the politicians who took part in the rally were Ampang member of parliament Zuraida Kamaruddin and Selangor state assembly speaker Hannah Yeoh.  The march was, however, blocked 100m before the Parliament gate by some 30 policemen at 11.15am.  Only a handful of representatives were allowed in to submit the group's memorandum.  Ambiga said the memorandum was received by Minister in the Prime Minister's Department Datuk Seri Dr Shahidan Kassim.

Protester Group Identity: Protesters opposed to a forthcoming rise in water prices
Notes: The upcoming rise in water prices saw about 100 people turn up at Hong Lim Park yesterday to protest against it. Notes: PHILIPPINE police opened fire as a protest by thousands of rice farmers who lost their crops turned violent yesterday, killing one and wounding about a dozen, a leader of a farming group said.  About 6,000 farmers blocked a portion of the main highway in North Cotabato province on the southern island of Mindanao, demanding government assistance after drought linked by some to 'El Nino' hit hundreds of thousands of hectares of farmland.  A farmer died on the spot and about a dozen others were wounded in the legs and shoulders, Capuyan said, adding the police first tried to disperse them with water cannon but started shooting when they held their ground.  North Cotabato Governor Emmylou Mendoza said about 20 police were wounded when the farmers attacked them with sticks and stones. She said the first shot was fired by the protesters.  "Any violation of national police rules and regulations shall be meted [out] with the appropriate penalty," national police spokesman Chief Superintendent Wilben Mayor said in a statement.  The protest began on Wednesday when farmers barricaded the highway in Kidapawan, demanding a dialogue with the governor and the release of 15,000 sacks of rice she had promised to them as relief.  In Koronadal, at least 2,000 farmers pushed back some 30 antiriot policemen who tried to disperse their rally. The law enforcers had to retreat to the Department of Agriculture office (DA) there.  The farmers padlocked the front doors of the DA building. The trapped policemen had to get out through the backdoor.  Ryan Lariba, a leader of the Bagong Alyansang Makabayan, which is supporting the farmers, said the 2,000 farmers gathered at the DA office to condemn what they said was the government's failure to address the plight of farmers stricken by the drought and its failure to provide immediate aid.  Anti-riot policemen, though outnumbered, tried to push the protesters back and used truncheons but the farmers stood their ground and were able to overpower the law enforcers.  A similar protest was held by farmers in Malaybalay City in Bukidnon.  At least 100 protesters have also been picketing the DA's regional office in Davao City since Wednesday.  Domingo Azures, regional chairman of the party-list group Anakpawis, said the protest action in Koronadal would be peaceful unlike the one in Kidapawan City, where two protesters and a bystander were killed when police opened fire on a farmers' barricade to clear a road being blocked by the protesters.  The rally in Malaybalay ended peacefully on Friday after the governor vowed to help the farmers.  Jun Benemerito, secretary general of the Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas-Bukidnon, said at least 4,000 farmers from different towns in the province gathered last week in Malaybalay City to demand aid.  In Koronadal City, Azures said farmers would continue the protest action until today.  South Cotabato Governor Daisy Avance-Fuentes appealed to the protesters to keep calm. She said, however, that "90 per cent of the protesters are not from South Cotabato".  Fuentes said rice would be distributed to farmers starting today.  In Davao City, at least 100 protesters gathered outside the DA regional office.  On Thursday, at least 500 farmers staged a rally outside the municipal hall of Alabel in Sarangani.

Notes: Protests took place yesterday in Manila over Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte's plans to honour the late dictator Ferdinand Marcos with a state burial.  About 2,000 people gathered in heavy rain to denounce Duterte's plans to move Marcos's remains from his northern hometown to the National Heroes' Cemetery in the capital, Manila, next month.  The protests yesterdays were joined by Marcos-era victims of torture and imprisonment as well as relatives of victims of extrajudicial killings, which historians say claimed thousands of lives.  Protesters shed tears during the three-hour protest and organisers launched a signature campaign to try to reverse Duterte's decision.  Dictator, is to have a hero's burial, 27 years after he died in exile in Hawaii. The Supreme Court of the Philippines said yesterday that Marcos, whose 20-year rule was notorious for brutality, theft and corruption, was entitled to be interred in the national Heroes' Cemetery near Manila, a burial ground for war veterans and martyrs.  The court decided by nine votes to five to reject appeals against the order by groups representing victims of oppression under the Marcos regime. Its ruling said that as a war veteran and former president, he met the criteria for burial at the cemetery, known as Libingan ng mga Bayani. "While he was not all good," the ruling said, "he was not pure evil either."  Activists protested outside the court in Manila. A group representing almost 40 anti-Marcos organisations said: "With this decision, the very definition of hero is now in question."  Dozens of students ran naked through their campus to protest against the burial of the former dictator Ferdinand Marcos at a cemetery for national heroes. Marcos, who ruled for nearly two decades, was buried with military honours last week almost 30 years after his death. The male students from the University of the Philippines, clad only in masks, held banners demanding the removal of the body.

As convoys of vehicles brought downtown Jakarta to a standstill, the protest turned violent, with taxi drivers jumping up and down on vehicles that refused to take part, drivers working for app-based services coming under attack, and some fighting back by hurling rocks.  The demonstration came after weeks of rising tensions between traditional public transport operators in the sprawling, traffic-clogged metropolis of 10 million and a flurry of new ride-hailing services.  Traditional taxi, motorbike taxi and other public transport drivers are angry that the new services are offering rides at lower prices, claiming they are not paying taxes, and are operating without official permits.  Jakarta police estimated that up to 6,000 drivers were involved in yesterday's protest, and 6,000 police were out on the streets for the protest.  Police officials vowed to take action against protesters who committed violence, but it was unclear if they had made any arrests.
